In total, the he scored 175 goals in 258 Premier League outings, having briefly also returned to the club on loan in 2012.

Reminiscing on the noughties era, Scott said: "This is the era where I really started watching Premier League football. And it was largely because of one man. Thierry Henry.

"The greatest Premier League football player of all time, in my opinion.

"People praise manager Arsene Wenger as the architect of modern football, as the mastermind behind the Premier League becoming what it is today. Well, if Wenger was the architect, Thierry Henry was the builder. He was the site manager.

7 Henry is regularly hailed as the greatest Premier League striker of all time Credit: Getty

"For me, the best player to ever play in the Premier League. He had everything: the pace, the strength, the grace, the way he'd open up and whip that ball into the bottom right-hand corner. Unbelievable.

"And most notably, think of the omissions in the noughties. No [Didier] Drogba, no [Wayne] Rooney, no Ruud van Nistelrooy or Cristiano Ronaldo. And that is how highly I rate Thierry Henry.

"And when you look at his goals, 30 goals in that invincible season.

But what people don't talk about is the season before: he got 24 goals and 20 assists.

"He had 74 career assists across his entire Premier League career. For me, unrivalled. The best Premier League striker in the noughties."

7 He was part of the squad that won the Premier League without losing a game Credit: Getty

Top 10 Premier League goalscorers ever Alan Shearer - 260 Harry Kane - 213 Wayne Rooney - 208 Mohamed Salah - 193 Andrew Cole - 187 Sergio Aguero - 184 Frank Lampard - 177 Thierry Henry - 175 Robbie Fowler - 163 Jermain Defoe - 162

2010s is a real tough one

You've got Wayne Rooney 'still being world-class', while Ballon d'Or nominated Harry Kane emerges as 'the best striker England have ever produced'.

According to Scott, you've also got Luis Suarez, 'who, for my money, is probably one of the best players to never win the Premier League.'

"But I'm going with Sergio Aguero," He added. "It's as simple as 184 goals in 275 appearances.

"And he provided what for me is the most iconic moment in Premier League history. 93 minutes, 20 seconds on the clock against QPR.

"United think the title is theirs. Sergio Aguero, enter stage left; the rest is history.

"For that and that alone, he's got to be the best striker in the Premier League in the 2010s."

7 Aguero's goal against QPR could be the most iconic in English football history Credit: AFP

Erling Haaland will go down as the greatest in history

Haaland has been making history and smashing all Premier League records since his arrival at Man City in 2022.

He has the title of being the fastest player ever to reach a tally of 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 100 goals in the Premier League.

The Norway international has also become the fastest player to reach 100 goal involvements in fewer than 100 league games (94).

Haaland, who also holds the record for the most goals ever scored in a single Premier League season (36), is the only player ever to score a hat-trick in three consecutive home league games.

The three-time Golden Boot winner became the first player to score 50+ goals in a top-flight season in England since 1931 in 2023.

7 Haaland has scored more than 300 career goals at just age 26 Credit: Getty

On the 2020s, Scott said: "This one's a little bit simpler because we've got the absolute phenomenon, the freak of nature. And the lovely guy, by the way; I love the cut of his jib, it's Erling Haaland.

"He's already scored 117 Premier League goals in 137 games. And he's got 24 assists to his name.

"36 goals in his opening season. I mean, unbelievable. I think that he will go down as possibly the greatest striker in Premier League history if he keeps scoring goals at this click.

"And if he stays at City and sees out his 74-year contract at the Etihad, then he might just overtake Alan Shearer's record.

"But for me, it's simple. Erling Haaland is the best striker of the 2020s so far, and you can't argue with it."

7 City are the only side with a 100 per cent record Credit: Getty

I need to pick a fifth

It's hard to pick four players because so many have to be omitted and so this is why it's a Mount Rushmore or less.

"I've missed out Andy Cole, Robbie Fowler, Luis Suarez, Harry Kane, Mo Salah, who arguably wasn't necessarily a striker, but he's one of the greatest to play in the Premier League.

"But for me, the fifth that I'm going to put carve another place for on the mountain is Wayne Rooney.

"208 goals, arguably the best football player England has produced in his generation. He did everything. He won it all.

"He was the engine room and the heartbeat and the soul of a lot of that Man United side under Fergie [Alex Ferguson].

"I just cannot ignore him. For me, he got me on the edge of my seat.

"He made me love watching Premier League football, even watching Manchester United. So Wayne Rooney is up there as my fifth in my Mount Rushmore-or-less of Premier League strikers."

Sports.title: Harry Kane confirms surprise career change plan and gives Bayern Munich contract update
Sports.content:
Harry Kane says he's close to signing a new contract at Bayern Munich - and after that a career in the NFL could await.

The England captain is in the final year of his Bayern deal, prompting speculation over his future with the European giants.

4 Kane is set to snub interest from Barcelona and Saudi Arabia to extend his stay at Bayern, who he signed for in 2023 Credit: Getty

However, he's set to extend his stay with them with Kane poised to sign a new deal which will keep him at the club until 2029.

“We're in good talks, I'll be honest. We're fairly close," the striker said.

"There are some things that we need to iron out. I'm happy there. I think it won't be too long before there's some sort of announcement.

"I feel really comfortable in the team, with the coach, the environment. I want to just be at this level, and push this level for as long as possible."

Kane's American dream

At 33 years old, Kane has half an eye on what comes in the next chapter of his life.

Some turn to coaching, some turn to punditry, but the former Tottenham star is keen on still competing in elite sport, playing with a different kind of football.

Having heavily hinted his next move in football could be in Major League Soccer, Kane added that that could work as a bridge towards him moving into American football as a specialist kicker.

He wouldn't be the first to switch from association football to American football; former pro soccer player Brandon Aubrey became the Dallas Cowboys' kicker.

Kane, who is also an avid golfer said on the prospect of playing in the NFL: “That is something I will try and look at a bit more seriously. It all depends on what happens in my career over the next five or six years, the motivation and what I want to do.

"The NFL is a lot more realistic than the golf one, let’s put it that way.

4 Kane is a lover of NFL and a fan of the New England Patriots Credit: Rex Features

“If people know I am still on the top of my game here with football it is not a conversation that would be had.

"Maybe if I am in MLS in the future or somewhere like that, it might be a thing where you could connect the two maybe with the seasons but again, it is in the back of my mind because right now, I am feeling that I want to play as long as I can.

“I think sometimes it is easy to get to my age, 33, you start thinking about retirement or the future but I am trying to extract everything I can from the last two, five or ten years, I will keep going.”

Kane's Ballon d'Or hopes

Before Kane tries executing his ambitious NFL plan, he has the potential to reach the very pinnacle of his first sporting love.

England's all-time record goalscorer is a huge contender to win the Ballon d'Or this year having hit 73 goals for club and country in a record-breaking 2025/26 season.

The winner of the ultimate individual accolade in the game being announced in London next month and Kane admits it would be 'unbelievable' to win it.

4 Kane is aiming to become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 Credit: AFP

“I know what I achieved last year was as good as anyone. So I don't want to shy away from that either. But ultimately, my mindset is to move on," he said.

“I think the timing of the Ballon d'Or is tough, because you're already in a new season, you're already focused on what I can achieve this year.

"And after every game you're talking about what you've done last year. So it's hard for me to get my head around that.

"But from my point of view, I've said, it would be unbelievable to win it, I'd be extremely proud to win it. I think I'm definitely in the running to win it, without a doubt.

"So time will tell, the voters will vote for who they want. Whether people doing more interviews or less interviews has an impact on that. It obviously has an impact socially, and on the debate around it, for sure.

"But the actual voters, I'm not 100 per cent sure. I think the voters will vote for who they think deserves it, and they'll have the information, the stats, and they'll decide.

4 Yamal, Kane and Mbappe are likely to be among the main contenders to win the award in 2026

"I think from my point of view, I've been happy… it makes me more proud when other people talk about me, when other teammates or ex-players or whoever it is, people who compliment me on what I achieved, I think that makes me more proud than me trying to talk about it myself."

The other main contenders for the gong are Real Madrid and France superstar Kylian Mbappe, as well as Spain and Barcelona star Lamine Yamal, who has a World Cup winners' medal to boast on account of Spain's triumph Stateside.

Although talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor is in no doubt that the award must go to Kane.

"Honestly, I'm tired of seeing on my timeline Lamine Yamal and Mbappe talking about how they deserve to win the Ballon d'Or," Agbonlahor said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"I love how Harry Kane's just quiet. Harry Kane's favourite, he's going to win it.

"But these guys… I don't like it. If I'm doing the votes, I'm like, 'Shut up.' You keep talking about it and that you deserve to win it, it's not going to make you win it.

"Harry Kane should win the Ballon d'Or, he's done the most."

Kane was speaking ahead of England's Nations League clash against Spain on Saturday night, live on talkSPORT, kick-off 7:45pm.

England also face Czechia twice and Croatia during this international break with these three matches also live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland has caused surprise food boom in Norway
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's influence reached new heights during the World Cup - it has even caused a surge in carrot sales in Norway.

If the Manchester City talisman wasn't a superstar before, this summer catapulted him into a new stratosphere as his goalscoring exploits and unique personality made him a household name.



3 Haaland finished as the World Cup's third-top scorer on his tournament debut Credit: Getty

On the pitch, Haaland led Norway to a World Cup quarter-final, firing in seven goals in six games before being knocked out by England.

And his profile only grew away from it, with the goal machine's lifestyle - which includes meditation and his unfiltered social media activity - earning him a whole new fanbase.

Haaland was easily the most viral player of the competition, whose Instagram following grew from 40million to 60million during it.



Haaland inspires Norway again

The 'Haaland effect' is showing no signs of slowing down in Norway, with reports that he is now inspiring a boom in carrot consumption.

According to reports, carrot sales have increased by 25 per cent in the Scandinavian nation in recent weeks, and isn't hard to trace the root cause.



The vegetables are a known favourite of Haaland's, who has previously been spotted snacking on them while signing autographs and he recently starred in a commercial promoting them.

During the World Cup, he featured on every Norwegian television channel in an advert for vegetable wholesaler Bama - a vegetable wholesaler, where he drives a truck and eats carrots.



Norwegian Nutrition Advisor Iselin Sagen told talkSPORT on the carrot boom: "The sales went up in July. We have never seen this record in July before.

"Also the sales were very good in August. And we know that there were two things going on at the same time in July.

"We had a big campaign with Haaland running before every match. He drives the trucks, eats the carrots and asks for more carrots.

3 Haaland has continued his goalscoring form into the new season, scoring five goals in his first five Premier League outings Credit: Getty



"And the supermarket also had bunched carrots on offer all summer.

"So, I cannot prove that it was him. But he is a huge role model in Norway and he was right in the middle of it."

This isn't the first time the 26-year-old's diet has caught the eye, having previously stunned fans by revealing he consumes 6,000 calories per day - which includes heart, liver and a cheat meal of kebab pizza.

But Sagen revealed Haaland's background, having grown up in the small farming town of Bryne, has likely led to his love of carrots too.

She said: "I really do think that Erling Haaland loves Norwegian vegetables.



"He grew up in a district where there are many farmers in Bryne, a small place in Rogaland district."

3 Haaland was inspirational for Norway at the World Cup, and he is a huge influence off the pitch too Credit: Getty

While the vegetables are in fact a staple in Norway, Sagen had little doubt that Haaland was behind their recent popularity, who is known to prefer bunched carrots with greens still attached.

The nutritionist continued: “We eat a lot of carrots in Norway. That's one of the most eaten vegetables in Norway.



"But we did know that bunched carrots with the grass on - that was having a low sale before this campaign, and this year.

"We were thinking about what's happening with the bunched carrots, [that] we should sell more.

"But when you ask how much is it [the increase], it's around 600 tonnes more carrots sold in July 2026 compared to 2025. And that's around one or two carrots more per person - we have five and a half million people in Norway."

Sports.title: Damning Kyle Walker verdict after being dropped by Burnley for last Championship game
Sports.content:
Kyle Walker has been a massive part of Burnley's terrible start to the season and deserved to be dropped for their last game.

This is the view of Joe Redmond from the Turfcast Podcast, who backed the decision not to play the club captain during their 1-1 draw at home to Burnley last weekend.

3 Walker is Burnley's club captain due to his vast experience Credit: Getty

The former England international is into his second season as a Burnley player with the Clarets sitting bottom of the Championship.

Burnley started the season as one of the favourites for promotion, but after eight games, they are the only team in the division without a win.

The Clarets have drawn four and lost four, including conceding a late equaliser at the weekend at home to the Rams.

It leaves them three points off safety and nine points off the final play-off place, which is eighth this year.

Walker has been playing as a centre-back for the majority of the season but after the 3-1 defeat at Swansea in September, he was dropped and didn't make it off the bench for the second time in the league this year.

On Burnley boss Nicky Hayden's decision to exclude Walker, Redmond told talkSPORT's EFL All Access podcast: ""No, "I think it was the correct decision to drop him personally.

"I do think he's been poor this season. He should be able to have a great influence on the squad, he has won literally everything that there is to win in club football.

"You cannot have a career better than Kyle Walker's, really. He has done everything. And obviously you've got to respect what he's achieved in the game and things like that. But ultimately, he has been a massive part of the problem.

"I do think some of it as well. I do feel sorry for Kyle as well in a certain aspect because he's been played out of position. Against Swansea, for example, we have three right-backs on the pitch. Obviously, Connor Roberts was at left back.

"Kyle Walker was at centre back. And Oliver Sonne was at right back. So I don't think it is just down to Kyle's poor performances, but I do think he has played poorly. I think it was the right decision to drop him against Derby.

3 Hayen is under increasing pressure and had declared the Derby match a must-win Credit: Getty

"And of course, the goalkeeper as well, Max Weiss, who had an absolute howler against Swansea and has done for the majority of the season. But Kyle has been poor. And if he hears this, I know that he would admit that as well. He would say that he has not been up to the standards that he would set himself.

"I did think it was a little surprising in the sense that he did a lot of media in the week leading up to it. He met up with the fan advisory board, he met up with some staff.

"He did loads of interviews with the rights holders saying, 'Yeah, we need to be better. We need to improve. We need to man up' is a term that he used just for him to be dropped. So that element of it was a little bit surprising.

"But I think what I said on my channel is when you look at the performances through the course of the season, has Kyle done enough to deserve to start against Derby County? For me, it is a no."

Clarets under pressure

Hayen has already admitted that he isn't sure he'll keep his job for too much longer.

When asked if he feared for his role following the draw to Derby, he said: "I understand the frustration of the fans; I understand that they're really disappointed – also, in myself, that they're fuming. I completely understand and I know how it goes in football, but... I'm honest and I tell the truth and I'm not hiding behind it.

3 Burnley's bad start to the season has been characterised by lots of poor defensive errors Credit: Getty

"There are a lot of reasons [for Burnley's poor start to the season] and you take this into account or you don't, and that's up to other people to decide...

"If we have 11 players, everyone thinks they're fit and they're fresh and they go for [it] 100 per cent, but the reality sometimes is different and you only know when you are on the inside.

"But I know I cannot claim a lot at the moment. I know that I'm responsible for it and if they [the club] make the decision that it's not good enough, then we'll see.

"But... I'm resilient; I was always a fighter. I will keep on fighting and... I'm 100 per cent sure that we can turn it around with these [next] three weeks, but we'll see what happens."

Burnley now have three weeks until they are back in action when they play Watford, who are also struggling.

And Hayen plans to take the Clarets away to a warm-weather training camp despite having eight players on international duty.

“So we will have a few days off for the players, where they really can switch off for football, leave the negativity behind and come back with fresh energy.

“We also have a running programme, because for us it's like a new pre-season, even if it's three weeks, but it will be important.

“So it's like you start with the running sessions, then we go on a camp, and then we have the preparation towards Watford.

“I can say again it's a must-win game, but this will be a week and a game where we want to show a really new face and a totally different one than now.”

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha reveals how Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has given him new tools to destroy defenders
Sports.content:
Rio Ngumoha reveals how Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has given him new tools to destroy defenders

Rio Ngumoha has his sights set on starring at Euro 2028, and Andoni Iraola’s influence could be key to this.

After a breakthrough 2025/26 season which culminated in a senior England debut, the Liverpool starlet's impressive start to this campaign has now earned him another international call-up.



5 Ngumoha is the youngest player in the England squad for their Autumn internationals Credit: Getty

Ngumoha was named in Thomas Tuchel's 27-man squad for the Three Lions' upcoming Nations League fixtures.

It represents a chance for the 18-year-old to make his competitive debut, having made his senior bow in a friendly win over New Zealand in June.

This followed Ngumoha's inclusion in England's pre-World Cup training camp, despite not featuring in their 26-man squad going to the tournament.



And after being earmarked as a star for the future with an impressive international debut, the teenager is now looking to stake his claim for a starting berth over the three weeks.

Ngumoha: I'm here to compete

Following his latest England inclusion, Ngumoha sat down with talkSPORT to discuss his goals for the international break.



With this his first involvement in a Three Lions squad, having previously been a training player for the pre-World Cup camp, the youngster revealed news of his call-up sparked huge celebrations in his family.

He told talkSPORT: "My mum was next to my brother - so I just called them and then they just started screaming down my phone.



“So it was an amazing moment."

But Ngumoha isn't just there to make up the numbers, as he insisted he is targeting a key role for England which will see him battle the likes of Marcus Rashford, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers for a starting berth on the left wing.

The Liverpool winger continued: “I've just got to come here and show what I can do to everyone and just make sure everyone just understands who I am.

5 Ngumoha looked a real livewire on his England debut against New Zealand in June Credit: Getty

"I'm not here just to be like a side part - I want to be a mainstay in the team and hopefully I can stay.



“But there's good competition everywhere. So it's about competing with the best players in the world now."

Euro 2028 dream

With his immediate goal breaking into Tuchel's starting XI ahead of some huge names, Ngumoha's long-term aim is ambitious too.

The prospect of a home European Championships in 2028 is sure to provide extra motivation for all English players, and not least Ngumoha, who will be almost 20 when it comes around.

Asked about the possibility of a home Euros, he admitted: “I'd definitely like to be a part of the squad.



“I think if I just keep doing what I'm doing, whether it's with the national team or at club level, if I just keep showing who I am and how I play and keep getting goals and assists and helping the team win trophies, then definitely I'd like to be a part of the team and hopefully we can go all the way as well.”

5 Ngumoha has continued to excite with his dribbling ability and direct style Credit: Getty

Iraola influence

Ngumoha's latest England call-up comes after after his continued involvement for Liverpool under new head coach Andoni Iraola.

The exciting winger burst onto the scene after being handed his big break by former boss Arne Slot, making 29 appearances last term and scoring twice in the Premier League.



He has remained a regular fixture since Iraola's arrival, featuring five times in all competitions this term, starting on three occasions.

And Ngumoha revealed the Spaniard's influence has helped him add a new string to his bow by playing him on the right wing, as well as his favoured left side.

Discussing life under the Spaniard, he told talkSPORT: “It's been good.

"The gaffer at Liverpool has really been helpful. And all the coaching staff as well - I can't speak highly enough of them.



5 Andoni Iraola heads into the international break still unbeaten as Liverpool manager Credit: Getty

“But I'm enjoying it. I'm playing left-wing, right wing as well. So it's given me another tool to destroy defenders."

Tuchel earns Ngumoha praise

Having handed Ngumoha his senior England debut at just 17 in the summer, Thomas Tuchel has made no secret that he is a huge fan.

After calling up the youngster for the September internationals, Tuchel shared his first impressions of him, as he said: “Rio was very impressive at this kind of age. He was explosive, he was adventurous, he was strong and one-on-ones like a true winger.



He added: “We are very excited about his potential and about his natural courage and adventurous style of play."

And Ngumoha was equally complimentary of the England boss, saying: “I don't even know what to say about the manager, Thomas.

“He's really helpful. And I think him picking me shows his belief in me, and how exciting and 'explosive' he thinks I am.

5 Thomas Tuchel could well see Ngumoha add to his one and only England cap in the coming weeks Credit: Getty



“All I can do now is just show him again why I should be here for the many more camps and why he thinks I should be a big part of the team and help the team."

Ngumoha could make his first England start when they face Spain at Wembley in the Nations League on Saturday night, live on talkSPORT, kick-off 7:45pm.

England face Czechia on two occasions during this international break and also take on Croatia with these matches also live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Manager’s mic drop moment could see Premier League club return to Europe for first time in eight years
Sports.content:
Manager’s mic drop moment could see Premier League club return to Europe for first time in eight years

Everton have been predicted to finish in a European position despite only having 18 outfield squad players.

David Moyes' side are only one of fives to remain unbeaten in the Premier League since the beginning of the season.



3 Moyes has led the Toffees to an unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign, so far Credit: Getty

The Toffees have had two wins and three draws from their first month of the campaign.

However, Evertonians will not be getting their hopes up following the anti-climax and downfall of recent years.

Everton were sat three points off a Champions League place but the season ended painfully as they went on to not win any of their final seven games.



Everton finished 13th, four points behind Brighton, who qualified for the Conference League, and five off Sunderland, who joined Bournemouth and Crystal Palace in the Europa League.

On the 'No BS' podcast, Max Scott said: "I'm giving Everton an A grade and I'm giving the board a D. Moyes is an A for what went well, but it would be even better if the board got their act together.



"That's the reality. What I love about Everton so far this season is that it is a case in point as to why David Moyes is still a top-tier manager.

"I don't care that some Evertonians don't quite like him or West Ham fans, I don't care what they think about his brand of football."



Everton's strong start, which also include two Carabao Cup victories, had been based on a solid defence.

Moyes' side have kept five clean sheets in seven matches overall and got the three points in their last match Ipswich with a 1-0 win.

Fury at board from Toffees fans

Despite a great start, Evertonians are experiencing a deep frustration against their owners, The Friedkin Group.

3 Everton fans have been hesitant on whether Moyes can help the team progress Credit: AFP



The Toffees released a portrait image of their squad for the season and it featured only 18 outfield players alongside only three goalkeepers, sparking concerns they'll lack resources as the season progresses.

Fans and the Everton Fans' Forum slammed the club’s recruitment after TFG pocketed over £100 million on deadline day.

They sold star player Iliman Ndiaye, top scorer Beto, Tim Iroegbunam, and Nathan Patterson, while a deal for Folarin Balogun collapsed.

Additionally, owner Dan Friedkin has faced fierce criticism for never attending a match or visiting Liverpool since completing the takeover in December 2024.



To make matters worse, the hierarchy had to call off a proposed £40million deal to sell midfielder and academy ace Harrison Armstrong following a backlash from the club's fans.

Supporters sang Armstrong's name throughout a draw at Bournemouth in August and said there would be a 'riot' if their brightest prospect was sold.

3 Armstrong has made five appearances and has one assist to his name this season Credit: Getty

Everton tipped for Europe despite setbacks

Scott added: "They are unbeaten in a Premier League, which so far has been uber competitive, with only a squad of 18 players.



"With the disappointment of the transfer window, with the whole Harrison Armstrong debacle, Moyes picked Armstrong, essentially put up two fingers to the board and then revved up the fans who started singing and they kept him at the football club.

"This is why you should never sleep on David Moyes. Never underestimate him. And I said at the start of the season, my prediction was that they'd get some form of European football.

"And despite all of the odds and all of the bad decisions from the club, they're on for that. I mean, I'm looking at the table now, they're seventh.

"They're ahead of Chelsea and all the multi-millions they've spent, ahead of United, ahead of Tottenham. I mean, I think they're a great example of if you've got the right manager, then you will go places."



Olly Clink responded: "Yeah, well-organized, hardworking, battle-hardened...

"And you mentioned that game against Bournemouth where he picked Harrison Armstrong. And it was after that game in the post-match press conference where he says, 'the fans know they've got an Evertonian as the manager.'

Scott added: "Yeah, it's like a mic drop moment."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo says he’s happy to sit on the bench as he makes retirement admission
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo says he’s happy to sit on the bench as he makes retirement admission

Cristiano Ronaldo has admitted that he considered stepping away from international football after the World Cup.

The Portuguese superstar endured yet more World Cup heartbreak in the summer as his nation were dumped out by Spain.



3 The World Cup has remained out of reach for Ronaldo Credit: Getty

Ronaldo led the line throughout, but they were no match for eventual champions La Roja, who saw them off in the round of 16.

Mikel Merino scored the only goal of the game, and Roberto Martinez departed.

Martinez had already announced that he wouldn't be staying on as manager of the Portuguese national team, but it was another failure for Ronaldo and co.



But new gaffer Jorge Jesus has called up the 41-year-old for this extended international break.

Portugal are in action four times over the three weeks, starting off against Wales in the Nations League.



And ahead of that contest at the Estadio Jose Alvalade, Ronaldo was asked if he'd considered calling it a day.

His response was very honest as he said: "Yes. I considered stepping away. I am always thinking about my future. I'm a thinker. This is why you see me here.



"I had a conversation with our president and our coach. I believe I can still help the national team reach to where they want. Also outside of football. This is a new generation, a young generation."

He added: "The critics will always be there... the most important thing is I know who I am. I know why the young kids especially love Ronaldo.

"I will continue to do that. I will continue to do that when I retire in ten years... I'm a happy person".

3 Ronaldo's legacy with the national team won't ever be surpassed but some feel he should call it a day



He also made it clear that he'll do whatever Jesus requires of him, even if it means he's not on the pitch.

Ronaldo said: “Whatever the coach needs from me with the national team, whether that means playing, coming off, coming on, coming off again, or even not playing at all... I am available.

"The pride I feel in representing Portugal is greater than that of any other international player”.

And for Ronaldo, there are two things left he'd like to achieve; winning the Nations League and reaching 1000 career goals.



On that, he said: “The missions now are two: winning the Nations League and reaching 1000 career goals”.

Continuation of an era

As it stands, the Al Nassr striker has appeared an incredible 233 times for Portugal and has scored 146 goals.

3 Ronaldo grabbed three goals at the World Cup to extend his record of scoring in every one Credit: Getty

This makes him the highest goalscorer at national level in men's professional football.



In terms of honours, he has the European Championship and Nations League to his name.

But the World Cup has more than likely evaded him, given he'll be 45 by the time the next one rolls around.

He has scored 11 times across the six World Cups that he's played in.

But Ronaldo refuses to deny that he could go on and on, saying: “Will this be my final chapter? Maybe, I don’t know. This could be my final season. But I don’t know.

“If my body allows me to, and if my mind does too, and if I’m still in good shape, then I don’t know. I don’t know what will happen”.



The race to 1,000 goals

That 1,000 career goal mark is getting closer and closer for Ronaldo.

The forward is on 979 career goals for club and country, and he has three for Ange Postecoglou's Al Nassr this season so far.

But if you look at his previous scoring rate in Saudi Arabia, Ronaldo has scored over 30 in each of his years there.

So, if he sticks to that rate, the 1,000 goals target will fall at some point this season.

And he can get there a bit quicker with a solid opening to the Nations League.



Portugal take on Wales, Norway on two occasions as well as Denmark with their first match against Wales on Thursday night, kick-off 7:45pm.

Sports.title: Idrissa Gana Gueye invests in top flight club with ex-Liverpool star in surprise announcement
Sports.content:
Idrissa Gana Gueye invests in top flight club with ex-Liverpool star in surprise announcement

Former Premier League midfielders Idrissa Gana Gueye and Lucas Leiva have become the latest athletes to invest in Le Mans FC.

It follows the club's return to the French top-flight earlier this year following a 17-year thanks to two successive promotions.



3 Former Everton and Aston Villa star Gueye has invested in Le Mans FC alongside ex-Liverpool man Lucas Credit: Getty

Le Mans had dropped as low as the sixth-tier after they were liquidated in 2013.

However, they now find themselves rubbing shoulders with the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Marseille once again.

Gueye and Lucas invest in Le Mans FC

There are also notable names within the club's group of investors, who have now been joined by Gueye and Lucas.



Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois and 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic are already shareholders.

Meanwhile, former Formula 1 drivers Felipe Massa and Kevin Magnussen have both invested.



Brazilian businessman Georgios Frangulis, who is engaged to world No.2 tennis ace Aryna Sabalenka, is also an investor.

Ex-Everton and Aston Villa man Gueye has now joined the club to help strengthen Le Mans' ties with African football.



The 36-year-old is Senegal's all-time leading appearance maker with 135 caps to his name.

Having left the Toffees in the summer, Gueye joined Saudi Pro League side Al Diriyah last month.

3 Le Mans were promoted to Ligue 1 after a 17-year absence last season Credit: AFP

Gueye and Lucas statements

In a statement, Gueye explained: "I am proud to join the Le Mans FC project as an investor.



"The club has a strong identity, genuine ambition, and a clear commitment to talent development.

"I look forward to putting my experience in French, English, international, and African football to work for the project and helping to strengthen its ties with Senegal and West Africa, particularly through the For Hope Campus."

Meanwhile, Lucas will work within player recruitment and development at the Stade Marie-Marvingt.

The Brazilian added: "I am very proud to join Le Mans FC alongside OutField and to be part of this new chapter for the club.



"Football has shaped my life and given me the opportunity to experience the sport at the highest level. Today, I want to put everything I've learned throughout my career to use in ambitious projects with a clear vision for the future.

"I deeply believe in what Le Mans FC is building. There is a history, an identity and real potential here, but above all, a shared ambition to build something sustainable and successful in the long term.

3 Leiva is set to work within recruitment and player development at Le Mans Credit: Getty

"For me, becoming a partner in this project means believing in its vision, contributing to its future, and helping Le Mans FC take the next steps in its history."



Lucas had spells with Brazilian club Gremio, Liverpool and Lazio before retiring in 2023.

The 39-year-old also won 24 senior caps for Brazil during his playing career.

Le Mans are currently ninth in Ligue 1 after claiming their first win of the season against Lorient on Saturday.

Patrick Videira's side face PSG at the Parc des Princes on October 10 in their first game after the international break.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney hits out at Benjamin Sesko for wearing 'little stupid shinpads' as Man United legend questions striker's shin injury in brutal takedown
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney has questioned why Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko sat out the club's 1-1 draw away at Fulham with a shin injury.

Rooney took to his podcast Stick to United to voice his displeasure with Sesko's absence from Sunday's game, implying that the Slovenian's shin injury was not serious enough to keep him out. 'Shin? Has he broken it?' said Rooney. 'You can hurt your shin, you can take tackles... I bet he's wearing them little stupid shinpads as well.'

The former United skipper did not stop there, later going on to say, 'If you're trying to play No9 [for Man United] and you've got a must-win game and you've got a sore shin and you're not playing... that's a big part of the problem.'

Later on in the show he reflected on his time at United, saying: 'Unless you physically can't play, you play when you're injured. I remember before games we used to get injections and the doctor used to put them in your arse.'

Two more former United players, Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt, also voiced their concern over the striker's omission from Sunday's squad.

Wayne Rooney did not mince his words when criticising the Slovenian international

Sesko has enjoyed purple patches in his short time at Old Trafford but has been unable to pick up consistent form

On their podcast, The Good, The Bad & The Football with Paddy McGuinness, Scholes aligned with his ex-teammate's view, saying: 'If it isn't broken, just wear your shinpads.' Butt then added: 'You're a player - you either break your shin or you don't play!'

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, the comments by Butt and Scholes did not go down well in Slovenia, with Leeds defender Jaka Bijol backing Sesko to rise above it.

‘I hope and believe that Beni knows how to distance himself from this kind of pressure,’ he said. ‘When things aren't going your best on the pitch and you have certain doubts, reading things like this can make your confidence even worse.

‘He shouldn't pay too much attention to it, since we all know what quality he has. He himself knows what kind of footballer he is, and I think he always shows it with incredible things on the pitch.’

Another of Sesko's compatriots, Zan Vipotnik of Swansea, also spoke out in defence of the forward as he said: 'It's not easy for him. Recurring physical problems are bad, and to add to that it messes with your head... I really hope and believe his absence from the pitch will be as short as possible and that things will turn for the best very soon.'

Sports.title: 'I'm not doing it for the money': Wayne Rooney reveals why he is pursuing punditry career after impressive World Cup BBC stint - and admits he may never return to the dugout again
Sports.content:
'I'm not doing it for the money': Wayne Rooney reveals why he is pursuing punditry career after impressive World Cup BBC stint - and admits he may never return to the dugout again

Wayne Rooney has revealed he turned to punditry to give him a purpose following his playing career, as he admitted he may never manage again.

The former Manchester United and England spoke of his move into punditry on the new Disney+ documentary The Real Rooneys.

Rooney is now an established Match of the Day pundit and impressed with his forthright views during the summer's World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

The 40-year-old joined the iconic football show at the start of the 2025-26 Premier League season, reportedly signing a £800,000-a-year deal.

Rooney had turned to punditry after unsuccessful spells in management, with his final two roles being short-term spells in charge of Birmingham City and Plymouth Argyle.

When showing off trophies won during his career – which had seen him score 253 goals for Man United and 53 for England – Rooney was asked why he had not retired outright.

Wayne Rooney has admitted he turned to punditry to give him a purpose following his glittering playing career

Rooney revealed the move into punditry as to give him a purpose after his playing career.

'I'm not doing it for money I'm doing it for a purpose rather than just being at the house all day,' Rooney said.

'There's a possibility I'll never manage again so moving forward.

'I need a role on The Masked Singer, but I'd get hammered'.

Rooney's last job in management came at Plymouth, where he was sacked with the club at the foot of the Championship table in December.

His dismissal followed a dismal run which had seen the Pilgrims win just four matches and suffer 13 defeats in 23 Championship games.

When asked by his wife Coleen whether he was sad about about losing the Plymouth job, Rooney responded: 'No I'm a realist I think you know as a player when your career is going to end and you can prepare for that.

'So the next stage in management for instance you don't know whether you'll be there a year, two years, 10 years or 3 months.

'Your not prepared when you lose the job.

Rooney acknowledged he may never manage again after several unsuccessful stints in the dugout

'I'm enjoying Match of the Day and it's time to learn and get better at what I'm doing.'

Rooney has since been one of the BBC's leading pundits during the World Cup, where he has earned praise for his development in his new career.

While typically giving his verdict on matches, Rooney entertained viewers by branding FIFA's World Cup final half-time show as 'c***', adding that he thought 'the best part was when it finished.’

Sports.title: Stars DO care about playing for England: Jarrad Branthwaite defends Declan Rice, Cole Palmer and Co after five dropouts cast shadow over start of Thomas Tuchel's post-World Cup mission
Sports.content:
Jarrad Branthwaite has defended his England team-mates amid a raft of withdrawals from the national team squad ahead of the upcoming Nations League fixtures.

Five key players have withdrawn from Thomas Tuchel's England squad before their international matches due to injury.

Cole Palmer, Declan Rice and Tino Livramento are among the absentees, along with Manchester United duo Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo.

James Garner and Morgan Gibbs-White have been called up as replacements.

Everton centre back Branthwaite, who earned his first cap under Gareth Southgate more than two years ago, dismissed suggestions that players are prioritising their clubs over their country.

The 24-year-old said: 'I think all players are fully committed to playing for England. I can speak for myself how much of a privilege is to to be in the England squad and to represent England, so I think it'll be the same for all the players.'

Chelsea midfielder Cole Palmer withdrew from the England squad to manage his workload

Branthwaite has struggled with injury issues of his own. Shortly after his first England appearance, he was linked with a move to Manchester United in the summer of 2024, but the club failed to meet Everton's £70million valuation. A groin operation and a thigh problem then sidelined him until October.

Last season, a hamstring injury delayed the start of his campaign until January, and another setback sustained in April limited him to just 10 Premier League appearances.

After a summer spent in Germany learning more about holistic fitness, Branthwaite has now played every minute of Everton's opening five Premier League matches and has earned his first call-up under Tuchel.

'When I went off with the injury (in April) I was devastated after the amount of times I’ve come back from it, and for it to happen again. To be called back up to the England squad means everything to me.

Jarrad Branthwaite is hoping to win his second cap after a solitary appearance in 2024

'All the hard work that went into the rehab to get to this point, it makes it worthwhile. I’m buzzing to be back in the England set-up.'

Branthwaite’s call-up marks an important first step in challenging Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa for a place in Tuchel’s starting line-up, and he revealed that the German coach’s main message to him was to ‘come in and express yourself.’

'Every time you get the opportunity you’ve got to show the best account of yourself to give yourself the best possible chance to be in the squad and in the team for the future,’ he said.

‘That starts with every training session, every chance you step on the pitch and hopefully I can do that.’

England face Spain in their first Nations League fixture at Wembley on Saturday, before two matches against Czech Republic sandwich Croatia away over an extended international break.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon says England can't EVER control games like Spain and must play to our strengths - because he's seen keeping possession 'is not in English DNA' after Barcelona transfer
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon says England can't EVER control games like Spain and must play to our strengths - because he's seen keeping possession 'is not in English DNA' after Barcelona transfer

Anthony Gordon believes England do not have the technical ability to replicate world champions Spain's football and has urged Three Lions fans to stop demanding a style of play that is at odds with the country's footballing identity.

The 25-year-old Barcelona winger scored the opener in England's World Cup semi-final against Argentina before Thomas Tuchel's side conceded two late goals to fall agonisingly short of reaching their first final since 1966.

Tuchel received widespread criticism in the wake of that defeat, particularly over his comments that keeping the ball is not within England's 'DNA', amid complaints about his negative tactics in the closing moments of the match.

Gordon, who has made an impressive start to life at Barcelona since his £70million move from Newcastle in the summer, now shares a dressing room with eight members of Spain's World Cup-winning squad. He insists he can offer a unique perspective now that he has crossed the divide.

'I think culturally it's not just that tournament or that game (against Argentina) where we couldn't control the game. England as a nation, we don't have that strength like the Spanish, where we control games like they do,' Gordon said.

'It's not in us, I'm not sure it's something that can be taught. I think playing in Spain, I can speak with an educated view, and the way they keep the ball is different. It's much different than I've ever experienced playing in this country. I'm not sure we can ever get that.'

Anthony Gordon believes England do not have the technical ability to replicate world champions Spain's football

The winger defended England boss Thomas Tuchel, who has face heavy criticism for the manner of their World Cup exit

Gordon believes playing for Barcelona has helped him realise the decision making of certain players in Spain is not a natural thing to English stars

Gordon firmly planted his flag in Tuchel's camp, using the exact same wording as he insisted that possession-based football 'is not in the English DNA'.

'I've only realised it to that extent from playing in Spain now, because I think we as English players are educated the same way as the Spanish players. We know how to keep possession, but it's the decision-making of certain players in Spain which just isn’t a natural thing (to us).

'I even look at some of the decisions (Spanish players) take on the ball sometimes and think, "I'm not sure how you've seen that." It's the way they're built; I don't know what it is, something that maybe we can't ever put a name to. They’re definitely built differently.’

The alternative, in Gordon's view, is to play to England's strengths, which he insists are good enough to compete with the best teams in the world.

'I feel like we are trying to replicate Spain. Because I'm in Spain now, I know we've got just as good players, but they have different qualities. Why try and make the (English) players the same as the Spanish players? Because the Spanish players lack the things that we have, and vice versa.

'I think we need to stop looking elsewhere as a country, and be proud of who we are, what we are, and the things we have, and stop comparing ourselves with other countries, because we're English. We're not Spanish or French, or other countries who have succeeded.'

Besides, Gordon insists English fans do not really want to see their teams play that way anyway.

‘Playing against Premier League sides who try and play ultra football, tiki-taka football, I always feel like the fans don't appreciate it as much,' he said. 'I feel like English fans want to see the English game, and in Spain they appreciate the Spanish style.

Gordon revealed he had never felt better than after opening the scoring for England in the semi-final against Argentina

He conceded he 'never felt worse 20 minutes later' after England's heartbreaking defeat

'The fans in England, they love a kind of basketball game, they love an athletic game, a direct game. When a team's losing, they don't want to see the team playing out from the back, they want to see a big striker winning headers and a bit of chaos. Maybe it's time to tune into that.'

Reflecting on the semi-final defeat to Argentina, Gordon described the emotional rollercoaster of opening the scoring before seeing England's World Cup dream slip away.

'I've never felt better in the Argentina game than when I scored that goal, and I've also never felt worse than 20 minutes later.’

He also ventured into 'what if' territory, suggesting England would have posed a greater threat to Spain in the final than Argentina ultimately did. Spain dominated the underwhelming final for possession and shots, finally converting through Ferran Torres in extra time as Argentina resorted to attritional tactics, as they had done days earlier against England.

'(England) got to the semi-final against the reigning world champions in a game which we should have won,' he said. 'In my opinion, we were the far better team for 60 minutes. OK, things took a turn and we didn't win, but that is football. Football's not perfect. Football doesn't mean you can be the better team for 60 minutes, you can score and you’re always going to win. Just in the moment we lost the game.

'I felt so confident. I felt like if we would have got to the final, I would have felt so confident playing Spain that we would come out victorious, but we just didn't get there, so we'll never know.'

Despite admitting his surprise at being substituted in the semi-final just 12 minutes after scoring, Gordon launched a staunch defence of Tuchel, insisting instead that the squad 'have to take responsibility' for their World Cup exit.

'Everyone likes to blame the manager, because that's football. But in my opinion, one person shouldn't be responsible for a million different decisions that are happening at one time.

'For me, we had the best team, we had the best players on the pitch in that semi-final, and in the last 20 minutes, we didn't play the best football. That's something the manager can't really affect from the sideline. So I think, as a group, everyone together should take responsibility. We shouldn't try to blame one man who's obviously trying his best to win the game and win the cup for us all.'

Sports.title: Man United reveal how much money they've SAVED with sacked boss Ruben Amorim taking over at AC Milan - as they try to rake in more cash by selling bits of the pitch for £125!
Sports.content:
Manchester United saved £8.5million when Ruben Amorim took over as head coach of AC Milan, the club’s latest financial results have revealed. United reported in May that the total compensation due to Amorim and his staff could rise to a maximum of £16.7m. But his appointment as Milan boss in June meant United have paid £8.2m, less than half that figure. Wednesday’s results also revealed that the cost of financing United’s debt has now rocketed past the £1billion mark since the Glazer family’s leveraged takeover. The club’s annual figures show that United paid £69.6m – an increase of £48.4m or 228.3 per cent from the previous year – in interest and other finance costs. The overall debt itself still stands at more than £1bn despite the cost-cutting measures imposed by minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos which contributed to United turning a £18.4m operating loss into a £22.6m over the last year. It consists of £577.6m of historic debt from the Glazer takeover in 2005, £111.4m owing on the club’s revolving credit facility and outstanding transfer fees. Ineos co-owned Man United have announced record revenue of £677.6m for the 2025-26 season The Americans’ £790m buyout has been the biggest factor in United bleeding over £1bn in the last two decades, and that infuriates fans who are fiercely opposed to the Glazers’ ownership and increasingly disillusioned with the Ratcliffe regime. After spending just £163m in the transfer market this summer – substantially less than many of their rivals – United are 12th in the Premier League table after one win in five games. The club are also at odds with large sections of the fanbase over their attempts to increase revenue and, more recently, crack down on ticket touts. It has also emerged that emails have been sent out to members and season ticket holders offering them the chance to buy miniature squares of the Old Trafford turf – which was re-laid in the summer for the first time in 14 years – for £125. United laid a new playing surface at the 'Theatre of Dreams' for the first time in 14 years over the summer, and the old pitch has been cut into 7cm x 7cm squares. Those squares have been packaged in acrylic cubes and are being sent out to supporters who want them in a smart black casing. The United website reads: 'Take home a piece of Old Trafford with this official turf cube, perfect for fans who want a keepsake from one of the most famous pitches in the world. 'Carefully preserved, this piece of turf makes a priceless memento of iconic games played at home and keeps the memories of match days alive. The sacking of Ruben Amorim in January cost the club £8.5million in compensation 'Perfect for gifting to passionate Reds, this turf cube makes a great addition to desks or can be displayed in a cabinet with other Manchester United collectibles.' The club have described the purchasable turf as a 'one-of-a-kind collector’s item' to club members and season-ticket holders in an email offering them 'exclusive' early access. Despite the huge debt and costs of servicing it, United are still committed to building a new £2bn stadium. The latest financial results revealed that the club spent £63.5m in June on a 25-acre triangle of land located 350 metres away from Old Trafford. While United were able to announce record revenues of £677.6m despite not playing in Europe last season, they reported an overall net loss of £43m – up from £33m last year – which sources say demonstrates the importance of maintaining financial discipline. Chief executive Omar Berrada said: ‘We are pleased to have secured record revenues which demonstrates the underlying strength of our business, particularly in a season without European football. United are selling small cubes of last season's Old Trafford turf to fans for £125 ‘This shows the direct impact of the work we have been doing over the past two years. It also proves Manchester United’s enduring popularity and commercial strength. ‘While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable.’ Commercial revenue for the year was down £16m and sponsorship revenue by £27.9m, partly due to United having no training kit sponsor following the end of their partnership with Tezos. The club have since signed a record £20m-a-year deal with Betway, as well as replacing sleeve sponsor DXC Technology with SumUp. Retail & merchandising revenue for the year was up £11.9m, and broadcasting revenue by £33.9m due to United finishing third in the Premier League after Michael Carrick replaced Amorim in January. Matchday revenue was down £6.8m due to the club’s shortest season since the First World War. Not playing in Europe and going out of both domestic cup competitions at the first hurdle meant that United played just 40 games.

Sports.title: 'We want to leave a legacy, to dominate English rugby': Inside Northampton's ambitious plan for back-to-back PREM titles - the curryhouse heart-to-heart, the former doorman solving their achilles heel and how they'll transform Franklin's Gardens
Sports.content:
In the heat of the summer holidays, Henry Pollock sprang a surprise on a couple of his team-mates in Mallorca.

Tommy Freeman and Fin Smith were visiting the Balearic Islands with their girlfriends and Pollock checked into a nearby hotel.

‘We decided to do a boat day on the Saturday,’ Freeman tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Most rental boats are small and slow but Pollock was like, “I’ve got a boat licence, which means we can get a quicker one”. We rocked up and got this huge RIB.

‘As soon as we got out the harbour, Pollock was like, “Bang! Gone”. We were going very fast and it was pretty scary. It was a good laugh. My hat fell off about three times and we had to loop back around for it.’

Pollock took the group around the south of the island, stopping off at a beachside restaurant for lunch.

It was around the time that Eddie Hearn, Pollock’s promotional agent, had made headlines by claiming the 21-year-old’s annual salary should multiply from £150,000 to £1million.

Northampton are ready for another strong season in the PREM, boosted by news that Henry Pollock has agreed a new contract

Pollock (left), Tommy Freeman and Fin Smith (right) soaked up the sun together in Mallorca - though had a distressing boat ride thanks to the England flanker

‘He got an earful about all the Hearn stuff,’ says Freeman. ‘Obviously there's a plan behind it all, but there's always a bit of stick, isn't there? It’s all good stuff. I might get my agent to come out and say I need a million, too!’

Pollock settled on a contract worth around £450,000. Despite the headlines, Hearn is yet to visit Franklin’s Gardens or the Northampton hierarchy.

Pollock discussed his ambitions with director of rugby Phil Dowson during the off-season – but the bulk of the negotiations were between recruitment boss Paul Shields and Stellar Rugby.

Locking down the youngster’s future was just one piece of Northampton’s business plan for the new season.

The club sold out 90 per cent of their PREM fixtures last season, thanks largely to the team’s effective and entertaining style of play.

Work is going on behind the scenes to achieve long-term sustainability. It is not feasible to expand the capacity of Franklin’s Gardens but the Supporter Village has been redeveloped over the summer, with enhanced facilities that can double up for corporate events.

There are also plans to move the team’s performance facilities out of the South Stand to create more space for commercial activity.

Coupled with a long-term vision to build a hotel on site, the club’s executives have been looking at matters far beyond Pollock’s contract extension.

The coaching team, Dowson and Sam Vesty, are tied into long-term deals and the RFU would have to pay a hefty fee to buy them out for potential roles with England.

‘Fundamentally, we are having a great time at Northampton,’ says director of rugby Phil Dowson

'We want to build a legacy,' says Alex Mitchell. 'We know we've got the squad and the coaches and the environment to do it. So why not go out and try to dominate?’

‘Fundamentally, we are having a great time at Northampton,’ says Dowson, when asked about the prospect of coaching England in the future.

‘We talk about the club flourishing, selling out, the village being renovated, the Saints Foundation having an impact in the community. From a personal point of view, at some point we would like to coach in international rugby because it is different.

‘Rugby’s different from the NFL. Bill Belichick stays at the New England Patriots because he's got nowhere else. There's no timeline on that.

'It's not just England. There's the opportunity to go and do something different, to test ourselves, either as a team or individually, to put ourselves under different pressure and to have new experiences.’

The immediate goal, however, is to secure back-to-back titles. In-house sports psychologist Oli Dixon has worked closely with the players to guard against complacency.

The club enjoyed a pre-season trip to Sri Lanka, where the new playing group bonded in unfamiliar surroundings. ‘All of the players went out for dinner together at a restaurant in Colombo,’ says scrum-half Alex Mitchell. ‘It was mainly curries. So spicy. Took my head off!

‘Fraser Dingwall started a conversation about how few teams have been able to go back-to-back. Saracens did it. We spoke about Wasps doing it with Lawrence Dallaglio and those guys. You look back on those teams and think, “What a team they were”. It’s a tough thing to do.

‘It would be quite cool if in 10 or 15 years, people look back at Northampton in the mid-2020s and say, "Oh, what a team they were”. That’s what we want to get after. We want to build a legacy. We know we've got the squad and the coaches and the environment to do it. So why not go out and try to go back-to-back and actually dominate?’

The club are already one of the finest attacking forces in Europe, often described as the All Blacks of English club rugby.

But they were presented with a humbling statistic over the summer: discipline. It is something they are looking to improve when they kick-off their campaign against Newcastle.

With the likes of Smith in their ranks, Northampton have become renowned as one of the finest attacking sides in Europe

Scrum-half Mitchell admits Saints' discipline is one of the few areas where they can improve

‘We were 10th for discipline,’ reveals Mitchell. ‘Penalties against us. We were 10th by quite some way, so that's one thing we want to try and rectify this year. We know we need to get better at not giving teams easy ins into our 22. Offsides, chat back, silly pens.’

The coaching team remains stable, although Jim Henry has moved into the role of defence coach, following Lee Radford’s departure to Scotland. Henry previously coached at Loughborough University, where he worked as a part-time doorman to supplement his sporting career.

‘Fundamentally, it's not a revolution,’ said Dowson. ‘It's an evolution of what Lee was doing. Lee came in and set a stall out in terms of our system and he set a stall out with an emotional point of view on what it means to defend. Jim's carried on both of those things. We just want to create a bit more pressure in defence. We want to create more turnovers.

‘We're probably defending for too long in phase counts. We want to get the ball back a little bit quicker. We want to have a bit more of an effort around post-tackle. You look at South Africa play, you look at Bordeaux, you look at Toulouse. Those two men on the tackle are making it tough to win fast ball and I think that's something that we can get better at.’

If Northampton can find another level after their title-winning campaign, they will prove difficult to stop.

Sports.title: Lewis Moody 'at peace' with MND diagnosis as former rugby star reveals hope his two sons will follow him into professional sport
Sports.content:
Lewis Moody 'at peace' with MND diagnosis as former rugby star reveals hope his two sons will follow him into professional sport

Lewis Moody said he would ‘absolutely love it’ if his two sons followed him into professional sport after eldest Dylan joined Arsenal ace Max Dowman in an England junior football squad.

Moody was a 2003 Rugby World Cup winner with England, earning 71 caps for his country. He also represented the British & Irish Lions and lifted 10 major trophies with Leicester Tigers.

Last year, the ex-flanker’s world was turned upside down when he became the latest former rugby star to receive a motor neurone disease (MND) diagnosis. MND affects the body’s nervous system. There is currently no cure.

Moody is not the only one with sporting talent in his family. Dylan, 18, is a goalkeeper for Championship side Southampton and alongside Dowman, is a current member of England’s Under-19 squad. Moody’s youngest son Ethan, 16, is a promising rugby player who is in Bath’s age grade set-up.

‘I'd absolutely love it,’ Moody said, when asked if he’d welcome Dylan representing England at senior level in football. ‘He’s got his professional contract and he’s doing really well with England.

‘He's got a lot of work to do until he gets to that stage, but he's got a great attitude and if he sticks at it and he really wants it, I'm sure he'll get where he wants.

Lewis Moody said he would ‘absolutely love it’ if his two sons followed him into professional sport

Dylan Moody, 18, is part of England's under-19 squad while his younger brother Ethan is a promising rugby player and is in Bath's age grade set-up

In a new documentary telling his MND journey, Moody has a series of tough, emotional conversations with his sons about his terminal diagnosis and the future

‘I’d like to think I’m supportive. I remember talking to Dylan and I asked him what he wanted to do. He said: “I want to play for England.” I had that classic adult response and went: “Is that a bit lofty?” But I apologised because it’s not my place to diminish his excitement. If that's his goal, I'm going to be there to support if he needs advice. I love the fact the kids are passionate about something they enjoy. Ethan is in the throes of the academy set-up with Bath. I’m excited.’

In a new documentary telling his MND journey, Moody has a series of tough, emotional conversations with both Dylan and Ethan about his terminal diagnosis and the future.

He also emphasises the need for further fundraising and awareness to support the bid to one day find a cure for MND.

Moody has taken part in a drug trial – funded by the My Name’5 Doddie Foundation, which was set-up by former Scotland and Lions star Doddie Weir who passed away due to MND in 2022. ‘I’m at peace with my diagnosis,’ Moody said. ‘I was at peace almost immediately.

‘There’s nothing I can do to change my circumstances, other than to use my energy to raise awareness so that the people who are fighting this disease have the resources they need so we can get to the outcome we all want. It isn’t far off.’

Lewis Moody vs MND was co-produced between 3 Rock Productions and TNT Sports. It premieres on TNT Sports 1 and HBO Max on Friday 25th September at 10pm

Sports.title: Alan Shearer and Graeme Souness back Flutter UKI's £500k Cash4Clubs fund with five grassroots clubs to be selected for huge £10k pot this year
Sports.content:
Grassroots sports teams and charities can now apply for a slice of £500,000 as Cash4Clubs, led by Flutter UKI and backed by footballing legends Alan Shearer and Graeme Souness, is back for 2027.

The flagship funding programme will help 225 community sports organisations in the UK and Ireland with two months to apply for grants of £2,000, with £10,000 grants also available for a lucky five of them for the very first time.

Launched in 2008, Cash4Clubs has boosted the local sport ecosystem by helping teams develop their facilities, buy new equipment and drive participation.

Last year's winners included Newcastle Panthers, an LGBTQIA+ football team, and Easthouses Lily Miners Welfare FC in Midlothian, with both being presented with their grants by Shearer and Souness, respectively.

'Seeing what this grant meant to Newcastle Panthers puts it all into perspective,' said Shearer.

'It’s helped so many members of our local community, both directly through the club and indirectly in the wider area through the positive message they share. I would encourage any neighbourhood club to apply for this grant.'

Cash4Clubs is back with £500,000 of funding available for sports teams to apply for

Alan Shearer backs the programme and awarded Newcastle Panthers with funding last year

Liverpool and Scotland legend Graeme Souness also backs the grassroots clubs funding scheme

Souness added: 'Never underestimate the difference a small grant can make to the survival of a grassroots club or local community group.

'Earlier this year, I visited Easthouses Lily Miners Welfare FC to surprise them at training with the news that they’d received a Cash4Clubs grant. Since then, they’ve battled back from financial hardship and the threat of relegation.

'The application window for Cash4Clubs grants, delivered by Sported UK, reopens on 1 October. If your club or organisation helps keep adults involved in sport, make sure you apply.'

During their nearly two decades of helping grassroots football, Cash4Clubs has directed over £7million into community athletics across the UK and Ireland. That includes £1.3million handed out to 640 clubs in just the last two years alone.

The allocation for this year once more focuses specifically on adult participation. They are targeting teams that tackle broader social issues, such as mental health challenges and economic deprivation, via the medium of sport.

Applications for the £500,000 funding allocation officially open on October 1, 2026.

For further information on Cash4Clubs please visit www.cash4clubs.org

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney slams Benjamin Sesko for missing Man Utd clash with shin injury
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney slams Benjamin Sesko for missing Man Utd clash with shin injury

Benjamin Sesko sat out of Manchester United's draw at Fulham, which has copped criticism from Wayne Rooney as the striker continues to deal with a shin injury

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney has raised issues with Benjamin Sesko's recent absence (Image: PA)

Wayne Rooney has cast doubt over Benjamin Sesko's shin injury, which continues to plague him, and claimed the Manchester United striker is likely wearing "them little stupid shinpads".

‌



The Slovenian has often been used from the bench this season having nursed the issue during the summer, but the striker was absent for the draw at Fulham after aggravating the issue in the Carabao Cup loss to Brighton.

‌



Sesko has by no means been a regular starter this term, a decision that has raised eyebrows given United's lack of genuine cover in that position, but missing the game at Craven Cottage meant Michael Carrick couldn't turn to him when he sought an equaliser.

‌



Rooney has been left bemused by the situation and the club's record goalscorer suggested the injury would not have been enough for him to sit out of the game. He said on his podcast Stick to United: "Shin? Has he broken it?' said Rooney. 'You can hurt your shin, you can take tackles... I bet he's wearing them little stupid shinpads as well."

‌



Rooney went on to add: "If you're trying to play No9 [for Man United] and you've got a must-win game and you've got a sore shin and you're not playing... that's a big part of the problem."

"Unless you physically can't play, you play when you're injured. I remember before games we used to get injections and the doctor used to put them in your arse."

United were able to rescue a point in west London after falling behind initially, but it still leaves Carrick with one win from his opening five games and pressure already building as the Red Devils sit 12th.

‌



View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko has continued to nurse a shin injury (Image: Getty Images)

With the club game taking a pause for the first international break of the campaign Sesko will be afforded some time to recover. The 23-year-old has withdrawn from Slovenia's squad for two Nations League matches against Scotland, plus their other games against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

"Manchester United can confirm that Benjamin Sesko has withdrawn from the Slovenia squad ahead of the upcoming three-week international break," a United statement said. "Benjamin will undergo tests this week before defining his individual recovery plan."

Sports.title: Should football fans be allowed to drink alcohol in the stands?
Sports.content:
Should football fans be allowed to drink alcohol in the stands?

Football fans have not been allowed to drink in the stands for decades but Prime Minister Andy Burnham is in favour of changing the law

View Image Football fans have had decades of nothing being able to drink from the stands

Andy Burnham has suggested he may look to remove the ban on drinking alcohol in the stands at football matches - which has stood since the 1980s.

‌



The Prime Minister has claimed the law is "unfair" for fans, given that those who attend other sporting events are allowed to enjoy a pint from their seats. Burnham, a big Everton fan, is still a match-going supporter. He insists there is a case for ending the ban, with rugby and cricket fans all allowed to drink pints from the stands.

‌



Burnham has long opposed the ban and said during his trip to the United States of America: “I don’t think it’s fair for football fans to be singled out in that way and I made that point. I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different. And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination.

‌



“There are different ways it could be done, perhaps on a trial basis. But I’m not going to back away from what’s been a long-held view of mine. I don’t see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently.”

It was made illegal in 1985 due to concerns about hooliganism. The fan-led review of football governance in 2021 called for the ban to be re-examined and suggested piloting the sale of alcohol within sight of the pitch in lower-tier English football.

Article continues below

The potential change has been welcomed by the Football Supporters’ Association and the English Football League, but police suggested it would be “incredibly rash” to make changes without considering their impact on safety.

Sports.title: Sensational Trent Alexander-Arnold return to Liverpool talked up as ex-England boss makes case
Sports.content:
Sensational Trent Alexander-Arnold return to Liverpool talked up as ex-England boss makes case

The case for Trent Alexander-Arnold to make a stunning return to Liverpool has been made

View 2 Images Liverpool have been told they could do with re-signing Trent Alexander-Arnold (Image: Urbanandsport/NurPhoto)

A repeat of Trent Alexander-Arnold's struggles at Real Madrid last season should leave the defender seeking a return to Liverpool. That's the opinion of former England boss Sam Allardyce, who believes the Reds are missing their former academy star.

‌



Alexander-Arnold, 27, hasn't set the world alight since joining the Spanish giants in a £10million deal last summer. The full-back struggled with injuries in his debut campaign and has played much of the current season as second-fiddle to Netherlands star Denzel Dumfries.

‌



He's started just two of Madrid's opening seven league games and was an unused substitute in their 2-1 defeat by Atletico Madrid this past weekend. Yet to stamp his claim as the long-term successor to Dani Carjaval, Allardyce said a reunion between Alexander-Arnold and Liverpool should be on the cards if he remains second-choice.

‌



Speaking on Footy Accumulators' podcast, No Tippy Tappy Football, the former Bolton and Newcastle boss said: "At 27, Trent still has years ahead of him. This is his prime. He’s at Real Madrid, and his experience there should stand him in good stead to be even better than he was when he left Liverpool, even though he hasn’t played as often as he would’ve liked.

"If he is going to be a Real Madrid player then this season he needs to be playing more than ever - if not, he should come back to the Premier League - Liverpool could do with him back. He’s capable of opening the opposition up."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool close in on Richard Hughes successor with FSG sporting director decision close READ MORE :

The full-back has long been criticised for his defending, but Allardyce doesn't believe he's inferior to other players in his position. The 71-year-old explained: "There have always been question marks over has defending, and rightly so, but that’s the same for most right-backs now. They stand with their hands behind the backs and don’t stop crosses.

"When Liverpool weren’t quite as good under Jurgen Klopp as they had been for a few years and they started conceding more goals, his defending got pointed out by everyone."

View 2 Images Sam Allardyce has called for the England star's return to Anfield (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Despite not yet becoming a regular starter for Jose Mourinho's side, Alexander-Arnold earned a recall to the England squad for their upcoming Nations League fixtures. Thomas Tuchel's decision was praised by Allardyce, given the full-back's unique abilities on the ball.

He added: "He’s not much worse than most other full-backs. His quality on the ball and ability to open up the opposition, whether it’s with short or long passes, are massive assets to England. I’m glad to see him back."
