World.title: Women Political Leaders Urged to Turn Electoral Influence into Local Governance Power
World.content:
BUCHANAN, Grand Bassa County — Twenty-six women leaders representing political parties across Liberia are participating in a weeklong leadership-development program aimed at strengthening their influence in local governance, public decision-making and political accountability.

The program, organized by the Netherlands Institute for Multiparty Democracy (NIMD), with support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Liberia, is being held in Buchanan City, Grand Bassa County.

It provides a cross-party platform for women leaders to deepen their understanding of local governance, exchange experiences and identify practical ways to influence decisions affecting their communities.

A key session, facilitated by Naymote Partners for Democratic Development Executive Director Eddie D. Jarwolo, focused on “Understanding Local Government Structures and Opportunities to Address Gender Issues.”

The session examined the evolution of local governance in Liberia, county-government structures, barriers to women’s participation, and emerging opportunities for women to assume greater leadership roles in public decision-making.

Participants explored the responsibilities of County Administrations, County Councils and local-development structures, while examining how women political leaders can engage in public consultations, influence County Development Agendas, monitor county budgets and development projects, and hold public officials accountable.

The discussions emphasized that women’s political participation must extend beyond elections and campaigning to the institutions where development priorities are set and public resources are managed.

Jarwolo stressed that local governance is where citizens experience the practical impact of democracy, including decisions on roads, schools, healthcare, markets, sanitation, security and economic opportunities.

“For Liberia, inclusive decentralization is not only about bringing government closer to the people; it is about bringing women closer to power, resources and decisions,” Jarwolo said.

He further challenged political parties to ensure that women who mobilize voters and support campaigns are also represented when policies, budgets and development priorities are determined.

“Women cannot continue to carry political parties during campaigns and remain absent when policies, budgets and development priorities are decided,” he said. “Women must be represented, heard and empowered to influence the local-governance decisions that shape their lives and communities.”

Jarwolo noted that women’s extensive experience in peacebuilding, conflict resolution and community leadership gives them valuable insight into the needs of local communities.

He said their increased participation in local governance could strengthen public trust, improve the responsiveness of local institutions and ensure that development priorities reflect the realities of families and communities.

The session also underscored the need for political parties to remain active in communities between elections, rather than limiting their engagement with voters to campaign periods.

Participants were encouraged to study their respective County Development Agendas, engage County Councils, participate in development-planning processes and monitor government commitments to local communities.

They also received simplified copies of the County Development Agendas to support their engagement with county-level development priorities.

The program further encouraged participants to build cross-party alliances around shared community concerns and advocate for reforms that expand women’s leadership from the community level to the national stage.

Jarwolo called on political parties to establish transparent pathways for women’s advancement at the community, district, county and national levels.

He said parties should invest in women’s political education, support qualified women for elected and appointed positions, and encourage members to remain connected to citizens between elections.

Emphasizing that “all politics is local,” Jarwolo said political credibility depends on leaders’ ability to understand citizens’ concerns, engage legitimate institutions and pursue measurable results.

He urged women political leaders to become more visible in county-governance processes by following budget allocations, monitoring development projects and assessing whether government commitments are delivering tangible benefits to ordinary citizens.

The session concluded with a call for women’s leadership to become more prominent in political parties, County Councils and development-planning processes, stressing that meaningful democratic participation requires women to have a voice not only in choosing leaders but also in shaping the decisions that affect their communities.

About the Facilitator

Eddie D. Jarwolo is Executive Director of Naymote Partners for Democratic Development. He holds a master’s degree in Public Sector Management and is an alumnus of The Hague Academy for Local Governance in the Netherlands. He has published on local governance, peacebuilding, and democratic development in Liberia.

World.title: Liberia: Dr. Yarkpawolo Takes Liberia’s Natural Resource Message to UN Platform
World.content:
Opening the event, Dr. Yarkpawolo said Liberia’s natural endowment presents the country with significant opportunities, but cautioned that the benefits of those resources depend heavily on how they are governed

NEW YORK, USA — Liberia’s natural-resource wealth should be managed as a foundation for peace, resilience and sustainable development rather than treated solely as an economic asset, Environmental Protection Agency Executive Director Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo has told an international gathering in New York.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

Dr. Yarkpawolo made the assertion Wednesday during a high-level Government of Liberia side event convened on the margins of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The meeting brought together government officials, United Nations representatives, development partners and experts to discuss the increasingly important connection between climate change, natural resources and conflict.

The event, held under the theme “The Nexus Between Climate, Conflict and Natural Resources: Pathways to Peace, Resilience, and Sustainable Development,” was organized by the Government of Liberia through the Environmental Protection Agency, in partnership with the United Nations Development Programme.

The engagement is taking place ahead of Liberia’s December 2026 presidency of the United Nations Security Council, with the organizers seeking to draw greater international attention to the links between environmental challenges, peace and sustainable development.

Opening the event, Dr. Yarkpawolo said Liberia’s natural endowment presents the country with significant opportunities, but cautioned that the benefits of those resources depend heavily on how they are governed.

He identified Liberia’s forests, minerals, rivers, fisheries and coastal ecosystems among the country’s most important natural assets, noting their potential to contribute to economic development and improve livelihoods.

But the EPA chief said the exploitation and management of those resources must be accompanied by strong institutions, transparency and meaningful participation from communities.

He warned that environmental pressures can compound existing social and economic difficulties, particularly in communities already affected by poverty, inequality and limited access to basic services.

Dr. Yarkpawolo said climate change can also place additional pressure on land, water and other resources, potentially increasing competition and tensions if institutions lack the capacity to manage those pressures effectively.

“Our natural resources are among Liberia’s greatest assets, but their value to the nation will depend on how responsibly and transparently we manage them,” he said.

He said government agencies and other stakeholders must therefore work together to ensure that resource management contributes to stability rather than creating new grievances among communities.

The EPA Executive Director emphasized that community involvement should be central to natural-resource governance, particularly because local communities are often directly affected by decisions involving forests, land, waterways, fisheries and other environmental resources.

“Communities cannot be treated as observers when decisions are being made about the resources upon which their livelihoods depend. Their participation is essential to building ownership, trust and lasting solutions,” Dr. Yarkpawolo said.

He further argued that stronger environmental governance could help Liberia confront climate-related risks while creating opportunities for sustainable economic activity.

According to Dr. Yarkpawolo, protecting natural resources should not be viewed as an obstacle to development, but as an essential component of development planning.

He said Liberia’s forests and coastal ecosystems, for example, have environmental functions that extend beyond their immediate economic value, including supporting livelihoods and strengthening the country’s resilience to climate-related impacts.

The EPA boss also stressed the importance of transparency in ensuring that citizens understand how natural resources are governed and how their economic benefits are distributed.

He said effective institutions are necessary to ensure that environmental regulations are enforced, resource exploitation is conducted responsibly and communities have avenues through which their concerns can be addressed.

The Wednesday gathering provided Liberia with an international platform to discuss how lessons from its peace experience could inform its response to emerging climate and environmental challenges.

Dr. Yarkpawolo said Liberia should use its peace as a foundation for addressing vulnerabilities before they escalate into wider social tensions. He noted that preventing environmental pressures from becoming sources of conflict requires early action, stronger institutions and cooperation among government, communities, international partners and the private sector.

The discussions also underscored the need for climate resilience to be incorporated into national development planning, particularly as Liberia seeks to maximize the benefits of its natural resources while protecting ecosystems.

The EPA Executive Director maintained that sustainable management of Liberia’s natural wealth requires a balance between economic development, environmental protection and the interests of communities.

The side event is expected to contribute to ongoing discussions on climate, peace and sustainable development while reinforcing Liberia’s role in international conversations on the governance of natural resources.

World.title: NCD Bids Farewell To Mr. B. William Yarsiah As He Departs Liberia For UK Chevening Scholarship
World.content:
Monrovia –The National Commission on Disabilities (NCD) has bid farewell to Mr. B. William Yarsiah, a prominent disability rights advocate and the Executive Director of the African Youth with Disabilities Network in Liberia and beneficiary of the prestigious UK Chevening Scholarship, as he departs Liberia to pursue a Master’s degree in Inclusive Education in the United Kingdom.

Prior to his departure on Monday, September 21, 2026, Mr. Yarsiah paid a courtesy visit to the NCD to express his profound appreciation to the Management and staff of NCD for the moral, financial, and institutional support extended to him throughout his scholarship application and preparation process.

Reflecting on his journey, Mr. Yarsiah said the process, which began in 2025, had finally come to fruition, expressing gratitude to everyone who contributed in various ways toward making his educational journey possible.

“I have come to the National Commission on Disabilities with my family to extend my thanks and appreciation to the Management and staff of NCD. Something we started in 2025 has come to fruition today,” Mr. Yarsiah said, thanking the Executives and staff members for standing by him throughout the process”. He noted.

He specifically acknowledged the support of NCD and through the leadership of Apostle, Dr. J. Aaron Wright Sr, noting that the Commission played an important role in assisting him with several aspects of his scholarship journey, including his English-language preparation and visa-related processes.

Mr.Yarsiah also expressed appreciation to individual staff members who contributed financially toward his preparations, emphasizing that their support would remain an important part of his journey.

As he prepares to represent Liberia in the United Kingdom, Mr. Yarsiah said he remains mindful of the responsibility associated with his opportunity.

He referenced a charged a charge from the British Ambassador urging him to remember that, as a Liberian and a person with a disability, he would be representing Liberia and the broader disability community.

“I am trusting that God gives me the wisdom and understanding to be able to come back with flying colors, so that Liberia will be proud of my performance in the UK,” he said.

In remarks, the Acting Executive Director of the NCD, Apostle Dr. J. Aaron Wright Sr., expressed appreciation for Mr. Yarsiah’s journey and encouraged he to remain focused on his studies and his responsibility to the disability community.

Apostle Wright used the occasion to encourage all persons with disabilities across Liberia to be inspired by Mr. B. William Yarsiah’s achievement and to pursue opportunities for higher education, professional development, and personal growth.

According to him the commission recognizes education as a powerful pathway to empowerment, leadership, self-reliance, and meaningful participation in national development. Mr. Yarsiah’s achievement demonstrates that persons with disabilities can pursue and attain opportunities that contribute to both individual advancement and the development of the nation.

The NCD boss also acknowledged a personal appeal made by Mr. Yarsiah concerning the welfare of his family during his period of study abroad.

Apostle Wright encouraged the Commission’s leadership, staff, and members of the disability community to continue identifying with and supporting Mr. Yarsiah’s wife and children while he is away.

“We are happy that you have reached this point, and we want you to know that your family remains part of our concern while you pursue this important opportunity,” the Executive Director emphasized.

Also speaking on behalf of the Commission, NCD Human Resource Manager, Madam Hannah, commended Mr. Yarsiah for his determination, commitment, and efforts in pursuing the scholarship opportunity, stressing that he is a proof of the slogan disability is not inability”.

She said the Commission was pleased to have supported his journey and expressed confidence that his academic pursuit would contribute to his personal development and the broader advancement of persons with disabilities in Liberia.

On behalf of the Management and Staff, Madam Hannah wished Mr. Yarsiah success in his studies and safe travels, while expressing hope that he would return to Liberia with valuable knowledge and experiences to contribute to national development.

The NCD recognizes education and professional development as important pathways for empowering persons with disabilities and strengthening their participation and leadership in national development.

World.title: Liberia: LACRA, Oil Palm Firms Move to Resolve Regulatory Disputes Through Joint Committee
World.content:
LACRA Director General Christopher D. Sankolo said the agreement demonstrates the importance of bringing regulators and operators together to discuss problems affecting the industry and identify areas where practical solutions can be developed

MONROVIA — The Liberia Agriculture Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA) and major oil palm concessionaires have agreed to establish a joint technical mechanism aimed at resolving regulatory concerns and improving cooperation within one of Liberia’s key agricultural sectors.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

The decision followed a high-level one-day dialogue on Wednesday, September 23, 2026, bringing together LACRA officials and representatives of major oil palm companies under the Liberia Agriculture Concession Association (LACA).

Rather than allowing regulatory disagreements and operational challenges to remain unresolved, the parties agreed to create a six-member Technical Committee that will provide a structured forum for examining concerns affecting the industry. The committee will consist of three representatives from LACRA and three representatives from the concessionaires.

The proposed committee is expected to undertake a broad review of the regulatory framework governing the oil palm sector, with particular attention to royalty obligations, quality control, regulatory compliance and export requirements.

LACRA Director General Christopher D. Sankolo said the agreement demonstrates the importance of bringing regulators and operators together to discuss problems affecting the industry and identify areas where practical solutions can be developed.

“The dialogue provides an opportunity for the regulator and concessionaires to sit together, understand the challenges confronting one another, and work toward common ground. Our objective is to strengthen regulation while ensuring that the practical realities of the sector are also taken into consideration,” Sankolo said.

Sankolo said sustained engagement between LACRA and concessionaires would be important as Liberia seeks to strengthen the performance and contribution of the oil palm industry.

He said the regulatory authority is prepared to work with stakeholders within its mandate to address concerns that could affect the effective operation of the sector, while maintaining the standards required by law and regulation.

“We believe that regular dialogue can help us address emerging issues before they become bigger challenges. LACRA remains committed to collaboration, compliance and finding workable approaches that can improve the regulatory environment for the oil palm industry,” Sankolo said.

Officials from LACA participated in the meeting, including its Chairman, Richard Fallah, while Elvis Morris, Vice President of Golden Veroleum Liberia (GVL), also attended. Representatives from Mano Palm Oil, Equatorial Palm Oil and Maryland Oil Palm were among the participants

The concessionaires used the meeting to raise a number of operational concerns, including theft affecting their activities and difficulties associated with obtaining additional land contemplated under their respective concession agreements.

Those concerns formed part of the broader discussion on how the government, regulators and concessionaires can improve coordination and create conditions that allow companies to operate more effectively while meeting their regulatory responsibilities.

The establishment of the committee also gives the parties an avenue to examine concerns surrounding royalty payments and other regulatory obligations in greater detail. Its work is expected to help clarify areas of the existing regulatory framework that may require further review or better coordination.

The committee’s Terms of Reference will be developed after the three representatives from the concessionaires are selected. Once constituted, the committee is expected to begin its work immediately.

The dialogue also placed emphasis on quality control and export compliance, areas that remain important to the credibility and competitiveness of Liberia’s agricultural commodities in both domestic and international markets.

Officials from LACA participated in the meeting, including its Chairman, Richard Fallah, while Elvis Morris, Vice President of Golden Veroleum Liberia (GVL), also attended. Representatives from Mano Palm Oil, Equatorial Palm Oil and Maryland Oil Palm were among the participants.

The new technical arrangement is expected to extend beyond the immediate concerns raised during Wednesday’s meeting by providing a continuing platform for discussions on policy, compliance, quality standards, royalties and other issues affecting the oil palm industry.

The initiative comes as stakeholders seek greater institutional cooperation in the sector and reflects an effort by the regulator and concessionaires to address their differences through dialogue while identifying measures that could strengthen the industry’s contribution to Liberia’s economy.

World.title: Pres. Boakai Re-nominates Kemah After IAA Named 3rd Top-Performing Public Entity
World.content:
Under DG Kemah’s leadership from 2022 to 2026, the IAA achieved significant institutional modernization and strategic alignment. Key milestones include developing the 2025–2029 Strategic Plan aligned with the Government’s ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development (AAID), executing major workplace renovations at headquarters, and expanding the agency’s workforce to 263 employees alongside 15 interns from the President’s Young Professional Program (PYPP) and the Ministry of Youth and Sports

MONROVIA – Achievements at the Internal Audit Agency (IAA) has not gone unnoticed as Director General David A. Kemah as Director General is retained by President Joseph Boakai in the position he served in the last four years.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

Kemah was re-nominated to the position for another four-year tenure as the Liberian leader on Tuesday, September 2, 2026 made new nominations in government.

Kemah, Certified Public Accountant (CPA), who holds an MBA from Nichols College, has led the agency since September 2022 – an appointment made by President Boakai’s predecessor.

The renewal of his mandate reflects strong executive confidence in his ability to continue safeguarding public resources and advancing fiscal integrity across state institutions.

Under DG Kemah’s leadership from 2022 to 2026, the IAA achieved significant institutional modernization and strategic alignment.

Key milestones include developing the 2025–2029 Strategic Plan aligned with the Government’s ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development (AAID), executing major workplace renovations at headquarters, and expanding the agency’s workforce to 263 employees alongside 15 interns from the President’s Young Professional Program (PYPP) and the Ministry of Youth and Sports.

Over 177 internal auditors across 97 public entities were trained in international standards, with staff earning professional certifications (CIA, LICPA, CFE) and advanced degrees.

Upon taking office, the Director General addressed a lack of women in leadership by actively promoting gender equality.

Under his leadership, women were appointed to several key executive positions—including Executive Director for Administration, Head of HR, Director for Quality Assurance, Director for Internal Audit, Head of Procurement, and County Sector Director—establishing a more inclusive and merit-based organizational culture.

Also, another key achievement witnessed the establishment of the audit recommendation and implementation unit, responsible to follow up on audit recommendations.

Kemah’s first term was marked by historic regulatory and technical breakthroughs in public financial oversight.

On June 25, 2026, he formally launched Liberia’s First-Ever Internal Audit Regulations—operationalizing the IAA Act of 2013—alongside a Public Sector Internal Audit Compliance Checklist and a National Compliance Scorecard.

To protect revenue, DG Kemah introduced the embossed IAA Validation Stamp to eliminate duplicate voucher processing, established transitory account reform MOUs with key financial institutions, and launched the ISOFT Audit Management System to automate risk assessments and audit planning.

These transformative reforms earned national recognition when the IAA was named the 3rd Top-Performing Public Sector Entity in Liberia under the Executive’s Performance

Management and Compliance System (PMCS), receiving the 2025 Performance Excellence Award from President Boakai in May 2026.

This re-nomination stands as a testament to the dedicated workforce at the IAA, whose personnel are currently deployed across 97 spending entities and seven counties.

Looking ahead, DG Kemah’s second tenure will focus on accelerating digital integration and expanding automated audit processes across the government.

With solid regulatory frameworks, modern oversight tools, and a trained workforce now in place, his continuation promises to reinforce institutional transparency and ensure public institutions fulfill the Agency’s core mantra of doing the right thing in the right way.

World.title: Liberia Pushes for Fairer Maritime Rules as Global Climate Talks Continue
World.content:
MONROVIA -Liberia is calling for a fairer and more practical approach to reducing greenhouse-gas emissions from international shipping, warning that the global push toward net-zero emissions must not create a heavy economic burden for developing countries.

The call came as Liberia presented its proposed alternative approach to the International Maritime Organization’s (IMO) Net-Zero Framework during a high-level engagement with United Nations Member States.

According to a press release issued by Liberia, the country supports efforts to reduce emissions from international shipping but wants the transition to take into account the economic challenges faced by developing countries.

The release said Liberia believes the transition “must be pragmatic, realistic, performance-based, affordable, scalable, equitable and legally coherent within the mandate of the IMO.”

Liberia, a major flag State and a developing country whose economy and history are closely connected to the sea, said climate action and economic protection should move together. A major concern raised in the press release is the possible effect of higher shipping costs on developing countries.

International shipping is responsible for transporting food, fuel, medicines, machinery, construction materials and other essential goods around the world.

The release warned that “significant increases in the cost of maritime transportation could have consequences beyond the shipping sector, potentially affecting food security, energy security, inflation, trade competitiveness and sustainable development.”

The press release said these possible economic effects should be considered alongside the environmental goals of maritime decarbonization.

It also called for country-specific economic impact assessments, noting that developing countries have different economic structures, trade patterns, technology, infrastructure and access to financing.

“Developing countries have different economic structures, trade profiles, technological capabilities, infrastructure, access to finance and levels of dependence on maritime transportation,” the release stated.

Liberia’s proposed approach focuses on measures that could help the shipping industry reduce emissions while limiting economic disruption.

According to the press release, the proposal includes commercially viable alternative fuels, improved technology and shipping operations, infrastructure development and capacity-building.

The release also called for support mechanisms for developing countries to be “predictable, transparent, equitable and genuinely responsive to the needs of developing countries.”

Liberia said developing countries should not be expected to carry major economic costs first and then wait for assistance afterward. Instead, the release stated that “the transition should be designed from the outset to minimize disproportionate economic consequences.”

The press release also called for evidence-based decision-making before new measures with major economic effects are introduced.

It said the IMO should consider the technical reliability, legal basis, affordability, availability and scalability of proposed measures and alternative fuels across different regions, ports and shipping routes.

The release said such considerations are necessary to build a framework that can gain the confidence of IMO Member States and be effectively implemented. “Net zero must not become a new burden on developing countries,” the press release emphasized.

Instead, Liberia said the transition should create opportunities for “investment, innovation, technology transfer, infrastructure development and capacity-building” while protecting trade, food security and sustainable development.

The press release made clear that Liberia is not calling for a reduction in global climate ambitions.

Rather, it said Liberia wants the maritime industry’s climate goals to be achieved alongside sustainable economic development. “Liberia does not seek to weaken global climate ambition,” the release stated.

The country said the IMO’s success will depend on the meaningful participation and confidence of all its Member States, including developed and developing countries, large and small nations, flag States and coastal States.

The release said Liberia will continue working with IMO Member States and other stakeholders toward a framework that is “environmentally ambitious, economically responsible and equitable for all Member States.”

The IMO and its Member States are expected to continue deliberations on the Net-Zero Framework during the next session of the Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC), scheduled for November 2026.

According to the press release, Liberia is expected to remain actively involved in the discussions leading up to and during the MEPC session, with the aim of contributing to an outcome that balances environmental goals with the economic realities of developing countries.

World.title: Liberia: Grand Bassa County Turns Over Five Motorbikes to Community Watch Forum
World.content:
Grand Bassa County— Grand Bassa County Superintendent Karyou Johnson has turned over five motorbikes to the Grand Bassa County Community Watch Forum to strengthen community-based security operations and support collaboration with the Liberia National Police (LNP).

By Francis G. Boayue

The motorbikes are intended to enhance the forum’s mobility and enable its members to work more closely with the police and other security institutions in responding to criminal activities across the county.

Speaking during the handover ceremony, Superintendent Johnson thanked the Grand Bassa Legislative Caucus, County Council and citizens of the county for supporting the establishment and operations of the Community Watch Forum.

Johnson also commended the leadership of the forum for its role in helping security authorities address the growing problem of illicit drugs in the county.

He said the forum had previously worked with the police, Drug Enforcement Agency and other security institutions to conduct operations, particularly around schools and communities where drug-related activities were reported.

“Today, the drugs in our county are not gone, but they have reduced,” Johnson said, crediting the forum for its contribution to efforts aimed at combating illicit drug activities.

According to the superintendent, the decision to provide motorbikes instead of direct cash support was intended to ensure that county resources provided for security operations result in tangible assets that can be used to improve service delivery.

Johnson said the county government would require organizations seeking operational funding to submit proposals and provide documentation showing how the funds would be used.

He described the provision of the motorbikes as a practical approach to supporting community security initiatives while ensuring that public resources are invested in visible and useful assets.

“The Community Watch Forum plays a very major role in the county in terms of assisting the police,” Johnson stated, adding that the motorbikes would enable the group to work more closely with law enforcement to pursue criminal activities.

The superintendent also highlighted several interventions undertaken by the county administration to support the justice and security sectors.

He cited the transportation of sick prisoners, construction of a court facility in Edina, provision of materials to the police, and renovations at the Magisterial Court and County Attorney’s Office.

He said the county government had also supported improvements at the police station and other justice-sector facilities.

He maintained that the county’s investments in the justice and security sectors were part of broader efforts to maintain peace and create an environment conducive to investment.

“We have been supporting the justice system in this county,” Johnson said, adding that the county’s security situation had improved.

He commended the Liberia National Police for its coordination of security operations in Grand Bassa County and thanked officers for their work in maintaining public safety.

At the ceremony, Superintendent Johnson formally handed over the key to the police commander, who was expected to subsequently present it to the leadership of the Community Watch Forum.

The initiative is expected to strengthen community policing and improve the forum’s ability to support law enforcement efforts across Grand Bassa County.

World.title: Liberia Set to Host 4th CoSPAL General Assembly
World.content:
L-R: House Committee Chair on Foreign Affairs Nehker E. Gaye and House Director of Press Robert Haynes

MONROVIA – The House Committee on Foreign Affairs says Liberia is set and ready to host the 4th General Assembly of the Conference of Speakers and Presidents of African Parliaments (CoSPAL) from Wednesday, December 9 to Friday, December 11, 2026, at the Farmington Hotel in Margibi County.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

The disclosure was made Wednesday during an appearance on the OK Morning Rush on OK FM by the House Committee Chair on Foreign Affairs, Nehker E. Gaye, and Director of Press and Public Affairs of the Honorable House of Representatives, Robert Haynes.

Chairman Gaye said the hosting of the continental parliamentary gathering follows recent engagements between the Liberian Legislature and the CoSPAL Secretariat.

According to him, the Head of the CoSPAL Secretariat, Amb. Dapo Oyewole, and a delegation were recently in Monrovia to assess preparations for the conference and formally sign the hosting agreement with the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Richard Nagbe Koon.

Chairman Gaye disclosed that the proposed theme for the 4th General Assembly is: “Enhancing Intra-African Trade and Investment through Legislative Leadership and Parliamentary Cooperation.”

He said the proposed theme reflects CoSPAL’s recognition of the role of legislative leadership and parliamentary cooperation in creating an enabling environment for increased intra-African trade and investment, economic integration, and sustainable development.

The Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman noted that the gathering will provide an opportunity for African Speakers and Heads of Parliaments to exchange views on issues affecting the continent and explore legislative approaches to advancing economic integration and development.

He further said the conference will create space for African legislative leaders to strengthen parliamentary cooperation and consider practical approaches to promoting trade, investment, economic integration, and sustainable development across the continent.

Commenting on the significance of the gathering, Press Director Robert Haynes said the 4th CoSPAL General Assembly will provide an important platform for African Speakers and Heads of Parliaments to deliberate on critical issues confronting the continent and identify practical solutions and implementation pathways.

He said Liberia’s hosting of the General Assembly presents an opportunity for the country to participate actively in continental parliamentary diplomacy and contribute to discussions surrounding Africa’s economic transformation and integration.

Haynes also disclosed that the Sub-Committee on Media and Publicity is working with local and international media institutions to ensure broad and timely dissemination of information ahead of the General Assembly.

As part of the public information campaign leading to the conference, Haynes announced that the House will, beginning in October, launch a special series on State Radio through the House’s public affairs program titled “The Road to Monrovia.”

The series will provide the public with information on CoSPAL, the significance of the General Assembly, Liberia’s preparations, the expected participation of African parliamentary leaders, and the broader objectives of the December gathering.

He said the media and publicity sub-committee will continue engaging both domestic and international media partners to ensure that the Liberian public and audiences across the continent are adequately informed about the conference.

The Conference of Speakers and Heads of African Parliaments (CoSPAL) brings together Speakers and Heads of African Parliaments to promote parliamentary cooperation, dialogue, coordination, and collective action on issues of strategic importance to the African continent.

The 4th General Assembly in Liberia is expected to bring together parliamentary leaders from across Africa for high-level discussions on legislative cooperation, intra-African trade and investment, economic integration, and Africa’s development priorities.

The Honorable House of Representatives says preparations for the December 9–11 General Assembly will continue in collaboration with the CoSPAL Secretariat, relevant government institutions, partners, and local and international media organizations.

World.title: EU Hails Zambia As “Beacon Of Democracy” But Presses Rule Of Law
World.content:
The European Union has called Zambia a beacon of democracy and promised deeper economic ties, while urging Zambia to keep respecting the rule of law. The two sides met on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York.

EU Commissioner for International Partnerships Jozef Síkela gave the praise at a bilateral meeting with a Zambian delegation led by Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Minister Mulambo Haimbe, who represented President Hakainde Hichilema. Brussels also recognised Zambia’s support for the UN Charter, multilateralism and the rules-based international order, and committed to what it called a forward-looking partnership built on shared values.

The two sides agreed that post-election developments should not divert attention from the chance to deepen economic cooperation. The delegation stressed what it described as the broadly peaceful conduct of the elections and thanked Brussels for sending an election mission, which deployed across the country at the invitation of the Zambian authorities.

Money was on the table as well. Zambia welcomed the EU’s Global Gateway initiative and development cooperation, including budget support of about €110 million. The partners agreed to align their cooperation with the Grow Zambia Agenda, with the focus on investment and value addition.

Brussels showed particular interest in Africa’s role in electric-vehicle battery and critical-mineral value chains, a field where Zambia’s copper and cobalt give it strong leverage. The two sides also agreed to keep working together on international peace and security.

The praise from Brussels comes at an awkward moment at home. The European Parliament has called for an independent and transparent investigation into the death of former Cabinet minister Mutotwe Kafwaya, who died during a security operation after the elections. Opposition leaders Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu remain in detention.

Mr Haimbe also used his time in New York to dismiss reports that Zambians had staged protests against their country at the Assembly. He said the delegation had been warmly received and the opening ceremony was well attended.

“There is no such thing as protests against Zambia,” he said. “Let us not listen to the allegations on social media that there is any sort of protest against Zambia.”

The minister said many Zambians living in the United States had told the delegation they were satisfied with the election outcome and happy about President Hichilema’s re-election. He called for national unity regardless of how people voted. “Let us continue talking about peace and unity. Let us live together,” he said. “Those who voted for and those who voted against, we are now past the election. Let us move forward.”

The statement was issued by Namatama Njekwa, First Secretary for Press and Public Relations at Zambia’s Permanent Mission to the UN.

Zambia also used the gathering to push its development agenda. In a message credited to President Hichilema, the delegation called for more investment in Africa’s digital infrastructure, computing capacity and skills, so that the continent can shape emerging technologies rather than only consume them.

The same message urged member states to turn the Pact for the Future, adopted in 2024, into measurable national results. “The pact was our collective commitment. Its implementation is our collective responsibility,” it said.

Mr Haimbe pointed to Zambia’s role in co-facilitating the Global Digital Compact and the Sevilla Commitment on development financing. He said this positions the country to help shape global digital cooperation and development finance.

The week also brought new diplomatic ties. Zambia established formal relations with the Principality of Andorra through a joint communiqué signed by Mr Haimbe, with tourism, education and climate action among the areas expected to benefit.

The minister also met Commonwealth Secretary-General Shirley Botchwey to discuss Zambia’s engagement with the Commonwealth on democracy, human rights, the rule of law, gender equality and environmental protection. Health Minister Professor Roma Chilengi attended the launch of the Accra Reset High-Level Panel report on reform of global health governance.

Mr Haimbe is scheduled to deliver Zambia’s national statement in the General Debate on Monday, and stronger multilateralism is expected to feature prominently.

World.title: Zambia can beat Algeria – Lungu
World.content:
South Africa-based striker Gampani Lungu is confident Chipolopolo can beat Algeria in Friday’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier away in Tizi Ouzou.

Zambia faces the Desert Foxes in a tough Group I encounter at the Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium, but Lungu says the team will not be intimidated by Algeria’s big reputation.

The Orlando Pirates winger, who has returned to the national team after an extended absence, believes Zambia can compete if the players remain united and match Algeria’s intensity.

Speaking after a training session at Tirsathone Stadium in Tizi Ouzou, Lungu said his return was long overdue.

“I want to thank God because I spoke some time back about it being God’s time. My not being in the national team was obviously preparing me for this moment,” he said.

Lungu said he is impressed with the new talent in the squad and is ready to use his experience to help the younger players settle.

“It is good to be back and to play for Mother Zambia, which is always an honour. I am also doing it for my family and the rest of Zambia, so I want to help the younger players and those who are new to the national team,” he said.

He acknowledged Algeria’s pedigree but said Zambia must approach the game without fear.

“Algeria is obviously a big nation and everyone knows them as one of the big teams on the continent. It is not going to be easy, but I don’t think we should put ourselves under pressure. At the end of the day, it is 11 versus 11 on the field. Anyone can win,” he said.

“Just because a nation has a big name does not mean they will automatically win. It is about the amount of fight we bring on the day.”

Lungu said the team’s preparations have focused on unity and fighting for each other.

“If we come prepared the way we have been preparing, and we all want to fight for each other, cover one another and fight for the nation, we can get Zambia to where it belongs among the top teams on the continent,” he said.

He also welcomed competition for places, saying it brings out the best in players.

“Everyone wants to play. For me, I always like competition because you can never be a great player if you don’t have competition.”

On his target, Lungu said he wants to deliver a goal for Zambia.

“I will do what I can for the country. For me, a goal is what I want for the country. We can’t win if we don’t score.”

Zambia face Algeria on Friday at 21:00 Zambian time.

World.title: Charge Mundubile And Zulu Or Free Them, Miti Tells State Over Kafwaya Death
World.content:
Human rights activist Laura Miti has challenged the Government to either take opposition leaders Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu to court or release them, warning that more than a month of official silence over the death of former Cabinet minister Mutotwe Kafwaya has left the State exposed to accusations of an unlawful killing.

Mr Kafwaya, an opposition figure, died during a security operation in the aftermath of the elections. More than a month on, Ms Miti said, the public still had no way of knowing what happened to him. “The State has been mute,” she said. “We need information from the State, and that information only comes when everybody who was arrested around that issue is taken to court, or when we are simply given the information.”

The burden, in her view, rests entirely with the authorities. A government that withholds information cannot complain when its own citizens and the international community reach “the very first conclusion” that a man was killed unlawfully, and every day the detainees spend out of court adds to the questions.

“None of us at this point can categorically say Mr Kafwaya was shot unlawfully. And that is wrong, because we are running into over a month now,” she said. “Why don’t we know? Why does the State find it possible to hold back this kind of information?”

The European Parliament has called for an independent and transparent investigation into the death. Ms Miti questioned who such an investigator would be in a matter involving the conduct of state security agencies, noting that even a commission of inquiry answers to the Government that establishes it. Zambia, she recalled, had once brought in British investigators in a matter she said involved former President Frederick Chiluba.

The deeper problem lies with the country’s institutions. “The fact that we do not trust the police, that we do not know whether we will ever be told the truth, should worry us. The fact that when you go to court, you are not sure whether the judge sitting there has been bribed should worry us,” she said. “Maybe the death of a former minister will be investigated in a manner in which the truth will never come out.”

Before any talk of foreign investigators, the activist said, the Government must take a step already within its power. “Right now, can Mr Mundubile and Mr Zulu be taken to court? Can the State give us the information it has?” she asked. “There are only two things that the State must do. Take the people to court or release them. You can’t have it both ways.”

Both roads carry a cost. Release without charge would leave the authorities answering why a man died, why people were arrested at all and why they spent so many days in cells. A prosecution on weak evidence, she warned, would invite the same reckoning: “Is this the evidence for which someone died? Is this the evidence for which you kept people in cells?”

Naming Mr Mundubile, Mr Zulu and Bishop Mwamba among those held, she added: “Government had better have evidence against these people, and had better be able to justify why someone was shot dead.”

Her message to the ruling United Party for National Development (UPND) was blunt. “The Government, the President, the UPND should know that if Mr Mundubile and Mr Zulu come out of those cells not having been taken to court, or the evidence adduced in court is flimsy, all of us in our minds will know that a great abuse of power has happened here.”

The case, she said, is long overdue. Asked whether the Director of Public Prosecutions was behind the delay, she said she did not know, but someone within law enforcement owed the public an answer. The silence of the first days after the death had already allowed speculation to run unchecked. “Someone needs to tell us why these people are not in court.”

Ms Miti was equally firm that the picture of Zambia painted abroad is overstated. The Government deserves to be “strongly criticised for what is true”, she said, pointing to the detentions and its conduct during the elections, including the closure of courts. Claims that the country is on fire or that citizens live in fear were not true, and army deployment at election time was nothing new, with soldiers seen on the streets in 2016 and 2021.

“You can become addicted to rage,” she warned. “The expression of outrage can become an end in itself, where you get used to saying this is wrong and you fail to interrogate it.”

Her sharpest words were for former diplomat Emmanuel Mwamba, on whom she said foreign voices were relying despite his habit of making up stories. “Emmanuel is a fugitive from justice. He actually probably should be extradited home to face his case.”

Zambians in the United States planning to protest at the United Nations General Assembly over the elections and Mr Kafwaya’s death had every right to do so, she said, and she would not call for them to be stopped. The protest would become a problem, however, if Mr Mwamba stood among them, given what she described as the disinformation he had spread on the matter.

The cancellation of passports belonging to certain individuals abroad drew equal criticism. “Governments should not throw tantrums. That is a tantrum,” she said. “Every action should have a goal. What is the goal? What have they achieved, other than bringing our name out there for discussion?”

Having spoken publicly since her twenties, Ms Miti ranked the UPND as the most thin-skinned government she had seen and the Movement for Multi-party Democracy (MMD) as the least. Both the Patriotic Front (PF) and the UPND, she said, had governed with the emotions of an individual, with vengefulness and insults coming from those who speak on the State’s behalf.

“Government is not a human being. Government should not have emotion,” she said. “Government must be able to allow citizens to criticise it, and criticise it viciously if they must, as long as citizens are not breaking the law.”

A caller from Lukulu took the opposite view, backing the passport cancellations and saying those who insulted President Hakainde Hichilema from abroad were insulting the millions who voted for him and should come home to answer. Ms Miti agreed that the personal attacks on the Head of State were “terrible”, adding that her own rule was never to write or broadcast anything she could not say to a person’s face.

On the detentions, her position did not move. No explanation has been given for why the case has not started, and Mr Mundubile and Mr Zulu remain in cells awaiting the State’s decision to charge them or let them go.

World.title: CBU, UCF sign MoU to build chemistry Laboratory
World.content:
The Copperbelt University and United Capital Fertilisers (UCF), a subsidiary of the Wonderful Group of Companies Limited, have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to undertake the construction of a state of the art chemical laboratory.

The agreement will also support training delivery, strengthen internship and scholarship programmes in chemical engineering, infrastructure, and other initiatives.

Speaking shortly after the signing ceremony, the Deputy Secretary to the Cabinet for Finance and Economic Development, Siakazongo Siakalenge commended the agreement between the two parties, noting that it highly aligns with the government’s economic and development vision through the ‘Growth Zambia Agenda’.

Mr Siakalenge emphasised that the MoU underscores the importance of developing a technologically skilled as well as an innovative human capital base, particularly in manufacturing and human capital with the aim of growing the economy.

“Especially in emerging sectors such as fertiliser manufacturing. Investing in human capital today lays the groundwork for a stronger, more resilient economy tomorrow,” he said.

He has since encouraged exploration of additional collaborations in advanced engineering and manufacturing sectors, which will contribute meaningfully to President Hakainde Hichilema’s developmental vision for Zambia.

In his welcome remarks, the Wonderful Group Chief Executive Officer, Roy Mwamba highlighted that the group is focused on the Grow Zambia Agenda aligned with the government’s vision, citing that the best investment is investing in people.

He mentioned that they had indicated earlier that their Urea fertiliser plant needed about 400 chemical engineers, disclosing that as the company continues to expand in just a few weeks to come the company will hold a groundbreaking ceremony of the expansion of the Amonia Urea plant at a cost of 1.5 billion United States dollars.

“With this expansion, there is a need for greater integration and Copperbelt University will collaborate closely with the group of companies to achieve this vision,” he said.

Earlier prior to the signing of the MoU, Copperbelt University Vice Chancellor Imasiku Nyambe stated that the MoU represents a crucial step in bridging the gap between universities and the industry.

Professor Nyambe commended the government for fostering collaboration between academia and industry, noting that President Hakainde Hichilema has continually championed such developments.

He also expressed gratitude to the Wonderful Group for their significant contributions to the country’s growth through substantial investments to be undertaken at the Copperbelt University.

Professor Nyambe, a beneficiary of industry scholarship further highlighted that CBU students will highly benefit from the increased professional exposure, scholarships and knowledge exchange to be implemented through the MoU.

“Opportunities, all of which will uplift their families, communities and the nation at large, he stated.

He noted that the construction of a chemical laboratory, a lecture theatre, and student accommodation will facilitate easier learning at the institution, emphasising that these developments are made possible by a supportive environment created through government efforts.

And Ministry of Education Permanent Secretary for Technical Services, Kelvin Mambwe, later emphasised that the MoU is highly significant, especially as it aligns with the Grow Zambia agenda.

Dr Mambwe highlighted that it provides students with valuable exposure to practical work opportunities, reaffirming the government’s commitment to education and initiatives that attach great importance to national development.

World.title: ZANACO launches 100m USD bond to support climate projects
World.content:
ZANACO has launched a 100 million United States dollars Medium-Term Note Programme that will support the issuance of sustainability bonds aimed at mobilising long-term capital for green and social projects in Zambia.

British Investment International (BII) offered technical support for the establishment of the bond Framework and has invested USS 15 million on the platform.

The programme will begin with an inaugural US$ 50 million sustainability bond, with further issuances expected over time.

The proceeds will be directed towards eligible projects in areas including renewable energy, climate-resilient agriculture, financial inclusion, affordable housing, healthcare, education and other initiatives with measurable environmental and social benefits.

Speaking at the launch at ZANACO Chief Executive officer Mukwandi Chibesakunda said the bank’s inaugural sustainability bond will go beyond raising capital, with proceeds expected to support climate resilience, economic growth and social development in Zambia.

Dr Chibesakunda said the bond, to be issued under ZANACO’s US$100 million medium-term note programme, has marked a shift from the bank’s earlier commitment to sustainable finance towards execution.

“At ZANACO, our purpose is anchored on our You First philosophy. It is a commitment that places our customers, communities and our country at the centre of every decision we make,” he said.

Dr Chibesakunda said the sustainability bond would create financing opportunities for farmers seeking to strengthen their resilience to climate change, entrepreneurs and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) looking to expand, as well as communities in need of critical social infrastructure.

She said the initiative was particularly important amid growing climate-related risks facing Zambia and other parts of the world.

Under the sustainability bond programme, ZANACO intends to channel financing towards climate-smart agriculture, renewable energy, energy efficiency, financial inclusion for SMEs and critical social infrastructure.

And British International Investment (BII) Managing Director and Head of Africa Chris Chijiutomi said the transaction was aligned with BII’s new five-year strategy, which places emphasis on strengthening the local financial system.

“One of the priorities of our new strategy that we launched this year is to help strengthen local financial systems and mobilize more private capital,” Mr Chijiutomi said.

Mr Chijiutomi said development finance institutions such as BII could provide investment, but greater mobilisation of private capital was necessary to expand development financing in economies such as Zambia.

He described the sustainability bond as an important milestone for Zambia’s financial sector and said it had the potential to encourage additional local and international investors and contribute to the development of the country’s sustainable finance market.

Africa.

Meanwhile, British High Commissioner to Zambia Rebecca Terzeon said the transaction demonstrated the UK’s shift towards an investment-led approach to development partnerships.

Ms Terzeon said BII’s investment in ZANACO’s sustainability bond showed how UK-supported development finance could be combined with Zambian institutions to support commercially viable investments while delivering development outcomes.

“This is exactly what the UK means when we talk about donor to investor,” Ms Terzeon said, referring to the mobilisation of finance to help businesses grow, create jobs and strengthen Zambia’s economic resilience.

Lusaka Securities Exchange (LuSE) Chief Executive Officer Nicholas Kabaso said the issuance marked a new chapter for Zambia’s capital markets and described it as the first sustainability bond issued by a Zambian bank.

Mr Kabaso said the exchange would work with stakeholders to develop a pipeline of future thematic bond issuances, simplify the issuance process and standardise reporting and verification requirements.

And Securities and Exchange Commission Director of Policy Development and Market Mateyo Lungu said the transaction was consistent with Zambia’s Capital Markets Master Plan, which seeks to develop innovative financial products and deepen the contribution of capital markets to national development.

Green Economy and Environment Minister Gilbert Siame said government supports initiatives that mobilise capital for climate-resilient and sustainable development.

Dr Siame said sustainable finance is important in financing the country’s transition towards a greener and more resilient economy, adding that the government was working to create an enabling policy and regulatory environment for climate finance.

World.title: Kabwe Court puts defilement suspect on defence
World.content:
The Kabwe Magistrates’ Court has found a 24-year-old man with a case to answer in a matter in which he is charged with defilement.

Kabwe Resident Magistrate Sebastian Mwenya has since put Levy Tebulo on his defence after the prosecution closed its case.

This follows testimony from the State’s final key witness, gynecologist Wisdom Banda of Kabwe Central Hospital, who told the court that he examined the complainant and found an injury to the hymen.

Dr Banda testified that the medical findings were consistent with a penetrative vaginal injury.

After considering the evidence presented by the prosecution, Magistrate Mwenya ruled that the accused had a case to answer and directed him to begin his defence.

“I have gone through the evidence presented by the prosecution and find you with a case to answer, therefore, I put you on your defense,” ruled the court.

The court heard that Tebulo is alleged to have had unlawful carnal knowledge of a girl under the age of 16 between February 3rd and February 14th, 2026, in Kabwe District.

After being informed of his rights, Tebulo opted to give sworn evidence in his defence and indicated that he would not call any witnesses.

“I’m going to give you a chance to go and prepare for your defence, and I wish you good luck,” said Magistrate Mwenya.

The matter has been adjourned to October 1st, 2026, for commencement of the defence case whilst Tebulo remains in custody.

World.title: Masebo’s petition case commences in the Lusaka High Court
World.content:
The petition hearing where former Minister of Lands and Natural Resources, Sylvia Masebo, is challenging the election of Annita Kamanga as Chongwe East Member of Parliament has commenced.

Ms Masebo, who stood on the United Party for National Development (UPND) ticket contends in her petition Ms Kamanga’s pre-election campaigns were characterised by conduct that contravened the Electoral Process Act and its Code of Conduct.

Robert Simeza is the lead lawyer for Ms Masebo in the petition case where 20 witnesses have been lined up by the petitioner to testify in court.

Four witnesses have so far testified that they were attacked by suspected supporters of the respondent, who in this case is Ms Kamanga.

One witness testified that he sustained body injuries as a result of the attack and that a medical report was issued at the hospital.

Both, the petitioner Ms Masebo and the respondent, Ms Kamanga, who stoon as an Independent parliamentary candidate, were at Lusaka High Court to follow proceedings.

Ms Masebo polled 6,798 votes against Annita Kamanga’s 16,058 votes in the August 13, 2026 general elections.

Some UPND supporters gathered at the Lusaka High Court grounds to show solidarity to the petitioner.

World.title: Chipangali drug stock stable
World.content:
The Department of Health Services in Chipangali District in Eastern Province has said that clinical services in the district are currently stable with drug availability above 89 percent.

Speaking during a senior management meeting held at the District Administration Office, District Clinical Care Officer Geoffrey Ndhlovu said the 89 percent drug availability in the district reflects adequate essential medicines, essential supplies and vaccines.

Mr Ndhlovu added that three more health facilities have been opened in the district bringing the total number of health facilities to 27.

“We have opened three more health facilities in the district namely Nguluwe, Nyauzi, and Kapatamoyo health facilities which are already providing outpatient health services,” Mr Ndhlovu said.

He however mentioned that the new facilities are not fully operational as they still face challenges relating to inadequate essential equipment and supplies.

“Currently we are not conducting deliveries in these new facilities, because the equipment we have can only support outpatient care,” he said.

He said the department has since requested for equipment through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), noting that the request was approved and awaits funding.

Meanwhile Mr Ndhlovu disclosed that the department has conducted 297 cesarean section surgeries from October 2025 to date.

He said the surgeries were conducted within the district at Muzeyi Clinic.

Mr Ndhlovu reported that all the surgeries were successful without any complications.

“All women who may require advanced care are referred to Muzeyi, so that they wait to deliver safely. So, the facility sometimes has inadequate space. In view of this, we are also lobbying for construction of a mother’s shelter and ablution block so that our mothers are well kept as they wait to be operated on,” Mr Ndhlovu said.
